incidents.title: Narada Tells of the Perfect Man
incidents.story: The sage Valmiki asked Narada if there lived a man who was truly good, brave, truthful and kind. Narada smiled and told him of Rama, prince of Ayodhya, who had all these virtues. He then shared Rama's whole story in brief. This talk planted the seed of the Ramayana in Valmiki's heart.
incidents.image: Sage Narada at the hermitage of Sage Valmiki requesting him to write the Story of Rama.jpg

incidents.title: The Cry of the Krauncha Bird
incidents.story: By the Tamasa river, Valmiki watched two krauncha birds singing together. Suddenly a hunter's arrow struck the male, and his mate cried out in grief. Filled with sorrow, Valmiki cursed the hunter, and his words came out as a perfect verse. From that pain of compassion, the first poem was born.
incidents.image: An illustration to a Ramayana series Valmiki and the death of the Sarus crane, India, Kangra circa 1775-1800.jpg

incidents.title: Brahma Blesses Valmiki
incidents.story: Valmiki wondered at the verse that had flowed from his grief. Then Lord Brahma appeared and told him it was by divine will. Brahma asked him to tell the story of Rama in this same verse form, and promised that all of it would be revealed to him. The poem would live as long as mountains and rivers last.
incidents.image: Agnipuruṣa rises from the sacred fire.jpg

incidents.title: Lava and Kusha Sing the Story
incidents.story: Valmiki taught the whole Ramayana to two bright young boys, Lava and Kusha. With sweet voices they sang it before gatherings of sages, who wept and rejoiced as they listened. At last they sang it in Rama's own court in Ayodhya. Rama listened with wonder to the story of his own life.
incidents.image: Valmiki instructs Kusha and Lava in the recitation of the Ramayana before the occasion of a sacrifice in Rama's palace(1).jpg

incidents.title: Dasharatha Longs for a Son
incidents.story: King Dasharatha ruled Ayodhya with justice, and his people lived in peace and plenty. Yet the king had no son to carry on his line, and this saddened him deeply. He decided to perform the great horse sacrifice to pray for children. His ministers and teacher Vasishtha gladly agreed to help.
incidents.image: Dasharatha and his sons return to Ayodhya.jpg

incidents.title: Rishyashringa Brings the Rain
incidents.story: Sumantra told the king an old story of the sage Rishyashringa, who had grown up alone in the forest. When the land of Anga suffered a terrible drought, King Romapada had the young sage brought to his kingdom. As soon as he arrived, rain poured down. He married the princess Shanta and was later invited to Ayodhya.
incidents.image: Sumantra summons Rama to Dasharatha's court.jpg

incidents.title: The Horse Sacrifice on the Sarayu
incidents.story: After a year of wandering, the sacred horse returned, and the great sacrifice was held on the northern bank of the Sarayu river. Priests chanted, gifts were given freely, and no guest went away hungry. Queen Kausalya and the others took part with devotion. Then Rishyashringa began a special rite for the gift of sons.
incidents.image: Vishwamitra brings Rama and Lakshmana to his hermitage.jpg

incidents.title: The Gods Pray to Vishnu
incidents.story: The gods were troubled by Ravana, who had a boon that no god or demon could kill him. In his pride, he had not asked for protection from humans. So the gods prayed to Lord Vishnu to be born on earth as a man. Vishnu agreed to come as the four sons of Dasharatha.
incidents.image: Sumantra summons Rama to Dasharatha's court.jpg

incidents.title: The Gift of Sacred Payasam
incidents.story: From the sacrificial fire rose a shining divine being holding a golden vessel. It was filled with heavenly payasam, a sweet rice pudding. He gave it to Dasharatha and said his queens should eat it to bear sons. The joyful king shared it among Kausalya, Sumitra and Kaikeyi.
incidents.image: Rama and Lakshmana with Sage Vishwamitra, circa 19th century CE,Datia Kalam of Rajasthani School of Art, Himachal State Museum,Shimla.jpg

incidents.title: Birth of the Four Princes
incidents.story: In time, Kausalya gave birth to Rama on a blessed day in spring. Kaikeyi gave birth to Bharata, and Sumitra to twins, Lakshmana and Shatrughna. All Ayodhya celebrated with music and dancing. The four brothers grew up wise and loving, and Lakshmana always stayed close by Rama's side.
incidents.image: Rama leaving for fourteen years of exile from Ayodhya.jpg

incidents.title: Vishwamitra Asks for Rama
incidents.story: One day the great sage Vishwamitra came to Dasharatha's court. Demons were spoiling his sacrifices, and he asked for young Rama to protect them. The king was afraid for his son, who was not yet sixteen, and hesitated. Vasishtha gently reminded him that Rama would be safe with such a mighty sage.
incidents.image: Rama, Lakshmana, and the Vishvamitra take leave of Dasharatha.jpg

incidents.title: The Mantras Bala and Atibala
incidents.story: Rama and Lakshmana set out with Vishwamitra, walking along the Sarayu river. On the way, the sage taught Rama two sacred mantras called Bala and Atibala. With them, the princes would never feel hunger, thirst or tiredness. That night they slept on beds of grass under the open sky.
incidents.image: Rama Killing Demon Tataka.jpg
incidents.artist: Ramachandra Madhwa Mahishi, Illustrated by Balasaheb Pandit

incidents.title: Rama Faces Tataka
incidents.story: In a dark forest lived Tataka, a fierce yakshini who had been cursed by sage Agastya and now terrorized the land. Rama did not wish to harm a woman. But Vishwamitra explained that a protector must stop such cruelty. When Tataka attacked with storms of stones, Rama struck her down and the forest became peaceful again.
incidents.image: Rāma slaying Tāṭakā.png

incidents.title: Gift of the Divine Weapons
incidents.story: Pleased with Rama, Vishwamitra gave him many divine weapons, celestial powers that appeared before Rama with folded hands. The sage also taught him how to call them back. Rama received them with humility and respect. These gifts would later help him protect the good and defeat evil.
incidents.image: Nainsukh - Rama and Lakshmana as Boys Assist the Sage Vishvamitra, Folio from a dispersed Ramayana series - 1976.14 - Metropolitan Museum of Art.jpg

incidents.title: Arrival at Siddhashrama
incidents.story: Vishwamitra led the princes to Siddhashrama, a holy hermitage. He told them that Lord Vishnu had once done penance there before taking the form of Vamana. As the small brahmin Vamana, Vishnu asked King Bali for three steps of land and covered all the worlds. Now Vishwamitra began his own sacrifice in that sacred place.
incidents.image: Indian - Rama Destroys Ogress - Walters W888.jpg

incidents.title: Maricha and Subahu Defeated
incidents.story: For six days and nights, Rama and Lakshmana guarded the sacrifice without sleep. On the last day, the demons Maricha and Subahu swooped down to spoil it. Rama's arrow hurled Maricha far away into the ocean, and another arrow ended Subahu. The sacrifice was completed, and the sages blessed the brave princes.
incidents.image: Rama and Lakshmana Confront the Demons Maricha and Subahu.jpg

incidents.title: The Daughters of Kushanabha
incidents.story: On the way to Mithila, Vishwamitra told the story of his family. King Kushanabha had a hundred lovely daughters. When they refused the wind god Vayu, he made their bodies bent, yet they forgave him with patience. Later King Brahmadatta married them, and at his touch they became whole and beautiful again.
incidents.image: The Birth of Sita - Raja Janaka of Mithila carrying her in his lap.jpg

incidents.title: Ganga and Uma Are Born
incidents.story: Vishwamitra spoke of Himavan, king of the mountains, and his two daughters. The elder, Ganga, was asked by the gods to come to heaven, and she went to bless the worlds. The younger, Uma, did great penance and became the wife of Lord Shiva. So both sisters became honored by all.
incidents.image: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana Cross the Ganga, Folio from a Ramayana series.jpg
incidents.artist: Painter from the First Generation after Nainsukh

incidents.title: The Birth of Kartikeya
incidents.story: The gods needed a commander to lead them against the demons. Lord Shiva's energy was carried by Agni and held by the river Ganga, and a radiant child was born among the reeds. The six Krittika stars nursed him, so he grew six faces. He became Kartikeya, the brave leader of the gods' army.
incidents.image: Gangā and the river Ganges falling from heaven, while S Wellcome V0045134.jpg

incidents.title: Sagara's Sons Search the Earth
incidents.story: King Sagara of Ayodhya began a horse sacrifice, but Indra stole the sacred horse. Sagara's sixty thousand sons searched everywhere, then dug deep into the earth to find it. Their digging troubled all creatures. At last they found the horse grazing near the great sage Kapila.
incidents.image: Sagara, a Vedic King and ancestor of Rama..jpg

incidents.title: Kapila and the Sixty Thousand
incidents.story: Thinking the sage was a thief, Sagara's sons rushed at Kapila in anger. The sage, a form of Vishnu, uttered one sound and they all turned to ashes. Later their nephew Anshuman found the horse and the ashes. He learned that only the holy Ganga flowing from heaven could free their souls.
incidents.image: Lord Rama with arrows.jpg

incidents.title: Bhagiratha's Great Penance
incidents.story: Generations passed, and King Bhagiratha left his throne to do hard penance for his ancestors. Pleased, Brahma agreed to send Ganga down to earth. But he warned that only Lord Shiva could bear the force of her fall. So Bhagiratha prayed to Shiva, standing on one toe for a whole year.
incidents.image: Sagara, a Vedic King and ancestor of Rama..jpg

incidents.title: Ganga Falls on Shiva's Locks
incidents.story: Proud Ganga rushed down from heaven, hoping to sweep Shiva away. But Shiva caught her in his thick matted hair, and she wandered there for many years unable to escape. Bhagiratha prayed again, and Shiva gently released her. Ganga then flowed to earth in sparkling streams.
incidents.image: Scene from Prabodha Chandrodaya Natakam.jpg

incidents.title: Ganga Reaches the Ashes
incidents.story: Ganga followed Bhagiratha's chariot across the land. When her waters flooded sage Jahnu's sacrifice, he drank her up, and released her only when the gods pleaded, so she is called Jahnavi. At last she flowed over the ashes of Sagara's sons, and their souls rose to heaven. Bhagiratha's devotion was complete.
incidents.image: Birth of Ganga on Earth.jpg

incidents.title: The Churning of the Ocean
incidents.story: At the city of Vishala, Vishwamitra told how the gods and demons churned the ocean of milk for nectar. They used Mount Mandara as the churning rod and the serpent Vasuki as the rope. When deadly poison rose, Lord Shiva drank it to save the world. Many treasures came forth, and finally the nectar of immortality.
incidents.image: The Sage Vishvamitra Requests from King Dasharatha the Assistance of His Son Rama.jpg
incidents.artist: Workshop active in the First generation after Nainsukh

incidents.title: Diti and the Maruts
incidents.story: Diti, mother of the demons, grieved for her lost sons and prayed for a son who could defeat Indra. Indra served her humbly during her long penance. Then, finding her careless one day, he entered her womb and divided the unborn child into seven parts. Diti forgave him, and the parts became the Maruts, the gods of the winds.
incidents.image: Indra maintains the celestial order by striking down the precocious Hanuman.jpg

incidents.title: Rama Frees Ahalya
incidents.story: Near Mithila stood the empty hermitage of sage Gautama. His wife Ahalya had been tricked by Indra, and Gautama cursed her to live there unseen, doing penance, until Rama came. When Rama and Lakshmana touched her feet, she shone again in her full radiance. Gautama returned, and the two were united once more.
incidents.image: Battle at Lanka, Ramayana, Udaipur, 1649-53.jpg

incidents.title: Janaka Welcomes the Sages
incidents.story: King Janaka of Mithila warmly welcomed Vishwamitra and the two princes to his great sacrifice. Janaka's priest Shatananda, the son of Ahalya, rejoiced to hear his mother was freed. Then Shatananda began telling Rama the amazing story of Vishwamitra's life. He said Vishwamitra had once been a mighty king.
incidents.image: Janaka, king of Mithila and father of Sita.jpg

incidents.title: Vishwamitra and the Wish-Fulfilling Cow
incidents.story: As King Vishwamitra traveled with his army, he visited sage Vasishtha's hermitage. Vasishtha's wondrous cow Shabala provided a feast for everyone. The king wanted the cow for himself and tried to take her by force. But Shabala brought forth countless warriors who defeated the king's army.
incidents.image: Varma - Vishvamitra Meditation.jpg

incidents.title: The Power of Vasishtha's Staff
incidents.story: Burning with shame, Vishwamitra did penance and won divine weapons from Lord Shiva. He returned and attacked Vasishtha with every weapon he had. Vasishtha simply held up his holy staff, and it swallowed every weapon, even the mighty Brahmastra. Vishwamitra realized that spiritual strength is greater than a warrior's might, and he resolved to become a brahmarshi.
incidents.image: Sīta addressed by the sage Vasishtha before departing with Lakṣmaṇa.jpg

incidents.title: Trishanku's Own Heaven
incidents.story: King Trishanku wished to go to heaven in his own body. Vasishtha refused, and his sons cursed the king. Vishwamitra kindly helped him and sent him rising up by the power of his penance. When Indra pushed Trishanku back down, Vishwamitra held him in the sky and created new stars around him, a heaven of his own.
incidents.image: Rama with his brothers studying in the Gurukula of Sage Vashishtha.jpg

incidents.title: Shunashepa Is Saved
incidents.story: King Ambarisha's sacrifice needed a victim, and he bought a boy named Shunashepa from his poor father. On the way, the frightened boy met Vishwamitra and begged for help. The sage taught him two sacred hymns to sing at the sacrifice. When Shunashepa sang them, Indra was pleased and granted him a long life.
incidents.image: Vishvamitra utters a curse.jpg

incidents.title: Menaka and Vishwamitra
incidents.story: Vishwamitra did deep penance at Pushkara. There the heavenly nymph Menaka came, and the sage spent ten years with her, forgetting his goal. When he awoke to what had happened, he did not blame her, but sent her away gently. Then he went north to do even greater penance.
incidents.image: Vishvamitra presents divine weapons to Rama.jpg

incidents.title: Rambha Turns to Stone
incidents.story: Worried by Vishwamitra's growing power, Indra sent the nymph Rambha to disturb him. Seeing through the plan, the sage grew angry and cursed her to become stone. At once he regretted losing his calm, as anger had spent his merit. He then vowed to give up anger and remain silent in penance.
incidents.image: At Indra's insistence, Rambha approaches Vishvamitra to distract the sage from his austerities.jpg

incidents.title: Vishwamitra Becomes a Brahmarshi
incidents.story: For a thousand years Vishwamitra held his breath and stayed silent, his calm never broken, even when Indra tested him. The gods and Brahma came and declared him a brahmarshi, the highest of sages. Vasishtha himself greeted him as an equal. Their old rivalry ended in friendship and respect.
incidents.image: Crossing the Ganges - Ramayana, Bala Kanda (1712), f.97 - BL Add MS 15295.jpg

incidents.title: Janaka Shows Shiva's Bow
incidents.story: Janaka told Rama about the mighty bow of Lord Shiva, kept in his family for generations. He also told how Sita appeared from the earth when he ploughed the field for a sacrifice. He had promised she would marry only the one who could string the bow. Many kings had tried, but none could even lift it.
incidents.image: Rama breaking the bow of lord Shiva in the court of Raja Janaka.jpg

incidents.title: Rama Breaks the Bow
incidents.story: The great bow was brought in a huge iron chest on eight wheels, pulled by many strong men. Rama lifted it easily and bent it to string it. With a sound like thunder, the bow broke in the middle, and the earth shook. Janaka joyfully announced that Sita would be Rama's bride.
incidents.image: Rama and Lakshmana on mount Prasravana, From the Mewar Ramayana.jpg

incidents.title: The Four Royal Weddings
incidents.story: Dasharatha arrived in Mithila with great joy, and the families honored each other's noble lineage. Rama married Sita, and Lakshmana married her sister Urmila. Bharata and Shatrughna married Mandavi and Shrutakirti, the daughters of Janaka's brother Kushadhvaja. The whole city celebrated as the couples walked around the sacred fire.
incidents.image: "The Death of King Dasharatha, the Father of Rama", Folio from a Ramayana MET DP107193.jpg

incidents.title: Rama Meets Parashurama
incidents.story: On the way home, the fierce sage Parashurama appeared, angry that Shiva's bow had been broken. He challenged Rama to string the bow of Vishnu. Rama calmly took it, strung it and set an arrow on it. Parashurama then knew Rama was Vishnu himself, bowed respectfully, and went back to Mount Mahendra.
incidents.image: While returning to Ayodhya Parshurama challenges Rama for breaking the bow of lord Shiva.jpg

incidents.title: Homecoming to Ayodhya
incidents.story: The royal party returned to Ayodhya, where the streets were decorated with flowers and banners. The queens lovingly welcomed their new daughters-in-law. Soon Bharata and Shatrughna went to visit their uncle in Kekaya. Rama and Sita lived happily, and their love grew deeper each day.
incidents.image: The people of Ayodhya mourn as Rama, Lakshmana, and Sita prepare to go into exile.jpg

incidents.title: Dasharatha's Wish for Rama
incidents.story: King Dasharatha, growing old, longed to see his beloved son Rama crowned as heir. He called the great assembly of Ayodhya, and the princes, elders and citizens all joyfully praised Rama's goodness and gave their approval. Delighted, the king fixed the very next day, under the star Pushya, for the coronation.
incidents.image: King Dasharatha cremates Shravana and his aged Parents.jpg

incidents.title: Ayodhya Decorates Itself
incidents.story: News of the coronation filled Ayodhya with happiness. People swept and sprinkled the streets, hung flags and garlands on every house, and lit lamps on the trees. All through the night the city hummed with music and excitement, as everyone waited to see their dear Rama become the prince-regent.
incidents.image: The people of Ayodhya and the celestial bodies are thrown into confusion by Rama's departure.jpg

incidents.title: Manthara on the Rooftop
incidents.story: Manthara, the maid who had come with Queen Kaikeyi from her father's home, climbed onto the palace terrace and saw the city glowing with celebration. When she learned it was for Rama's coronation, she was filled with jealousy and hurried down to Kaikeyi with bitter news.
incidents.image: Kaikeyi and Manthara - M. V. Dhurandhar.jpg

incidents.title: Kaikeyi's First Joy
incidents.story: When Manthara told her that Rama would be crowned, Kaikeyi was overjoyed and gave the maid a beautiful jewel as a reward. She said Rama was as dear to her as her own son Bharata. At first her heart was full of love and free of any envy.
incidents.image: Kaikeyi vilap.jpg

incidents.title: Manthara's Poisoned Words
incidents.story: Manthara would not give up. She frightened Kaikeyi, saying that Bharata would be sent away and she would become Kausalya's servant. Then she reminded the queen of two boons Dasharatha had once promised her, when she saved his life in the war against the demon Shambara. Slowly, Kaikeyi's good heart was turned.
incidents.image: Rama welcomed.jpg

incidents.title: The Sulking Chamber
incidents.story: Following Manthara's advice, Kaikeyi threw off her jewels and garlands and went into the chamber of anger. She lay on the bare floor in a soiled garment, scattering her ornaments around her. There she waited for the king, determined to win what she wanted.
incidents.image: India, Pahari Hills, Kulu School, late 17th-early 18th Century - Scene from the "Shangri" Ramayana (History or Rama) - 1996.361 - Cleveland Museum of Art.jpg

incidents.title: A Promise Sworn on Rama
incidents.story: Dasharatha came happily to share the good news, but found his queen lying on the ground. Worried and loving, he begged her to tell him what was wrong. He swore by Rama, dearer to him than life, that he would grant her any wish. Kaikeyi called the gods to witness his promise.
incidents.image: "The Death of King Dasharatha, the Father of Rama", Folio from a Ramayana MET DT236869.jpg

incidents.title: The Two Boons
incidents.story: Then Kaikeyi asked for her two boons. First, Bharata must be crowned in Rama's place. Second, Rama must go to the Dandaka forest for fourteen years, living as a hermit dressed in bark and deerskin. Hearing this, the king was struck with shock and fell senseless to the ground.
incidents.image: Rama learns of Kaikeyi's orders for Bharata's investiture and his own exile.jpg

incidents.title: A King's Night of Sorrow
incidents.story: All night long Dasharatha wept, pleaded and fell at Kaikeyi's feet. He asked how he could send away a son who had never done any wrong. But Kaikeyi stood firm and reminded him that a king must keep his word. The long, painful night slowly passed, and dawn came.
incidents.image: Kaikeyi told Dasharatha that he must fulfil her wish.jpg
incidents.artist: by Ramachandra Madhwa Mahishi, Illustrated by Balasaheb Pand

incidents.title: Sumantra Calls Rama
incidents.story: At sunrise, while the city waited for the coronation, the minister Sumantra was sent to bring Rama to his father. Rama set out at once in his chariot, cheered by crowds along the way. No one in the joyful streets knew what sorrow waited inside the palace.
incidents.image: Lakshmana and Sumantra guard Rama and Sita, who rest on the bank of the Tamasa River.jpg

incidents.title: Rama Accepts with Calm
incidents.story: Rama found his father crushed with grief, and Kaikeyi told him of the boons. Without any anger, Rama said he would gladly go to the forest to keep his father's word. His only sadness was that the king had not told him himself. His face stayed calm, like the moon untouched by trouble.
incidents.image: Ramayana - Pages 9 and 10.jpg

incidents.title: Kausalya's Grief
incidents.story: Rama went to his mother Kausalya, who was praying for his welfare. When he gently told her he must go to the forest, she fell to the ground like a tree cut down. She wept that she had waited so long for joy, and now must live without her son.
incidents.image: Rama meets Kausalya.jpg

incidents.title: Lakshmana's Fury
incidents.story: Lakshmana blazed with anger at the injustice and wanted to fight for Rama's right to the throne. Rama calmly held him back. He said that this was the working of destiny and that obeying their father was true dharma. He asked Lakshmana not to blame Kaikeyi.
incidents.image: Hanuman's monkey army, Rama and Lakshman in front of the castle in Lanka.jpg

incidents.title: Kausalya's Blessing
incidents.story: Seeing that Rama's mind was firm, Kausalya wiped her tears and prayed for him. She performed sacred rites and called on the gods, the forests, the rivers and the stars to guard her son. She blessed him that the dharma he so faithfully followed would protect him always.
incidents.image: Bharata and Shatrughna come to console Kausalya.jpg

incidents.title: Rama Tells Sita
incidents.story: Sita was waiting happily for the coronation when Rama came home pale and quiet. He told her he was going to the forest and asked her to stay in Ayodhya. He gently advised her to serve the elders and to treat Bharata with kindness while he was away.
incidents.image: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana leaving the palace of Ayodhya for exile.jpg

incidents.title: Sita Will Not Stay Behind
incidents.story: Sita would not hear of being left behind. She said a wife shares her husband's life, and that the forest with Rama would be sweeter than any palace. When Rama spoke of the forest's dangers, she wept and insisted. At last Rama agreed, moved by her love and courage.
incidents.image: Rama Sita Playing.jpg

incidents.title: Lakshmana Asks to Come
incidents.story: Lakshmana fell at Rama's feet and begged to go with him. Rama asked him to stay and care for their mothers, but Lakshmana said he could never live apart from his brother. Rama agreed and asked him to bring the divine bows and weapons kept at their teacher Vasishtha's house.
incidents.image: Rama, Sita, and Lakshman in the jungle (6125129762).jpg

incidents.title: Gifts for All
incidents.story: Before leaving, Rama and Sita gave away their wealth. They gave jewels, cows, silk and gold to the brahmins, to Vasishtha's son Suyajna and his wife, to their teachers and to faithful servants. No one who came to them went away with empty hands.
incidents.image: Rama and Sita, with Lakshmana returning to Ayodhya.jpg

incidents.title: Trijata Throws His Staff
incidents.story: A poor brahmin named Trijata came to Rama for help. Smiling, Rama asked him to throw his staff as far as he could. With all his strength the old man flung it across the river Sarayu. Rama gave him all the cows up to where it fell, and kindly said it was only a playful test.
incidents.image: Rama, Sita, and Lakshman in the jungle (6125129762).jpg

incidents.title: Farewell to Father
incidents.story: Rama came to take leave of his father. Dasharatha, broken-hearted, begged him to stay even one more night. He even told Rama to take the throne by force. But Rama refused, saying he would not let his father's word become false, and asked only for his blessing.
incidents.image: "The Death of King Dasharatha, the Father of Rama", Folio from a Ramayana MET sf2002-506a.jpg

incidents.title: Sumantra Speaks Out
incidents.story: The loyal minister Sumantra could not bear to see the king's suffering. He spoke frankly to Kaikeyi, telling her that she was hurting her own husband and the whole kingdom. He begged her to give up her demand, but Kaikeyi would not change her mind.
incidents.image: Ramayana - Pages 9 and 10.jpg

incidents.title: Garments of Bark
incidents.story: Kaikeyi brought out garments of tree bark for the forest. Rama and Lakshmana calmly took off their royal clothes and put them on. Sita, who had never worn such clothes, struggled with the bark and looked to Rama with tears, and he lovingly tied it over her silk.
incidents.image: King Dasharatha Approaches the Sulking Kaikeyi's Chamber (6125133208).jpg

incidents.title: Sita Goes as a Princess
incidents.story: The sage Vasishtha sternly rebuked Kaikeyi, saying that Sita had never been asked to live as a hermit. The king ordered fine clothes and jewels for Sita for all fourteen years. Kausalya embraced her and gave her loving advice, and Sita promised to stand by Rama always.
incidents.image: Hanuman finds sita in Ashoka vana A painting from Akbar Ramayana.jpg

incidents.title: Sumitra's Blessing
incidents.story: Queen Sumitra blessed her son Lakshmana as he left. She told him to think of Rama as his father Dasharatha, to think of Sita as his own mother, and to think of the forest as Ayodhya. Then she sent him off with love to serve his brother.
incidents.image: Rama, Sita, Lakshmana in exile in forest having a meal, pahari painting.jpg

incidents.title: The Chariot Leaves Ayodhya
incidents.story: Sumantra drove Rama, Sita and Lakshmana out of the city. Crying people ran after the chariot, and Dasharatha and Kausalya followed on foot, calling out to Rama. The old king fell into the dust as the chariot disappeared, and the whole city was filled with weeping.
incidents.image: Bharata returning to Ayodhya with Rama's padukas - sandals.jpg

incidents.title: The Night at Tamasa
incidents.story: Many citizens and brahmins followed Rama out of love and camped with him beside the river Tamasa. Rama did not want them to leave their homes for the forest. Before dawn he quietly drove away with Sumantra, hiding the chariot's tracks, and the grieving people returned to Ayodhya.
incidents.image: Meeting of Rama and Parashurama, from the Mewar Ramayana.jpg

incidents.title: Guha's Welcome
incidents.story: At Shringaverapura on the banks of the Ganga, Rama met his dear friend Guha, king of the Nishadas. Guha welcomed him warmly and offered him his kingdom and fine food. Rama thanked him with love but, keeping his forest vow, accepted only food for the horses and slept on the ground.
incidents.image: Rama, Sita, and Lakshmana at the Hermitage of Bharadvaja- Folio from a Ramayana Series (IA mma rama sita and lakshmana at the hermitage of bharadvaja folio from a ramay 37955).jpg

incidents.title: Lakshmana's Night Watch
incidents.story: While Rama and Sita slept on a bed of grass, Lakshmana stayed awake with his bow. Guha offered to keep guard so he could rest, but Lakshmana said he could not sleep while his brother lay on the ground. The two friends talked sadly through the night about Ayodhya's sorrow.
incidents.image: Rama, Sita and Lakshman at the Sage's hut (6124573733).jpg

incidents.title: Sumantra Sent Home
incidents.story: In the morning Rama and Lakshmana matted their hair with banyan sap, like forest hermits. Sumantra begged to stay with them, but Rama sent him home to comfort the king and show Kaikeyi that they had truly gone. With a heavy heart, the faithful minister turned back.
incidents.image: Rama and Sita, Hanuman, and Rama's three brothers Lakshmana, Bharata, and Shatrughna.jpg

incidents.title: Sita's Prayer to Ganga
incidents.story: Guha brought a boat, and the three crossed the holy Ganga. In the middle of the river, Sita folded her hands and prayed to the goddess Ganga to protect her husband. She promised to worship the river with offerings when they returned safely after fourteen years.
incidents.image: The Nawab of Murshidabad's boats on the Ganga (6125141004).jpg

incidents.title: The Sage at Prayaga
incidents.story: Near the meeting of the Ganga and the Yamuna, the travelers reached the hermitage of the sage Bharadvaja. He welcomed them lovingly and offered to let them stay. Rama wished for a quieter place far from the city, so the sage guided them to the beautiful hill of Chitrakuta.
incidents.image: The Kewat Pleads With Rama Not to Step on His Boat.jpg

incidents.title: Crossing the Yamuna
incidents.story: The brothers built a raft of logs and bamboo and spread soft grass for Sita. As they crossed the Yamuna, Sita prayed to the river for Rama's safety. On the far bank she also bowed to a great banyan tree and asked for its blessing, while Lakshmana picked flowers for her.
incidents.image: Rama travels with Sita and Laxman.jpg

incidents.title: A Hut at Chitrakuta
incidents.story: At Chitrakuta, among flowering trees and singing birds, they met the sage Valmiki. Lakshmana built a strong hut of wood and leaves. After performing the proper rites, Rama, Sita and Lakshmana entered their new forest home, happy in the beauty of the hills.
incidents.image: Bharata welcoming Rama, Sita, Lakshmana and Hanuman to Ayodhya by Raja Ravi Varma.jpg

incidents.title: Sumantra's Sad Return
incidents.story: Sumantra drove the empty chariot back into Ayodhya. When people saw that Rama was not in it, they cried out in grief. Even the horses shed tears. Sumantra told Dasharatha of Rama's courage and of his messages, and the king's sorrow grew deeper.
incidents.image: Rama leaving for fourteen years of exile from Ayodhya.jpg

incidents.title: The Story of the Young Ascetic
incidents.story: Late at night, Dasharatha told Kausalya a sad secret. As a young prince he once shot an arrow toward a sound by the river, and struck a young ascetic, remembered in later tellings as Shravana, filling water for his blind parents. The grieving father cursed him to die sorrowing for a son.
incidents.image: Bharata welcoming Rama, Sita, Lakshmana and Hanuman to Ayodhya by Raja Ravi Varma.jpg

incidents.title: Dasharatha's Last Night
incidents.story: Remembering that old curse, Dasharatha knew his end was near. Calling out Rama's name and longing to see him one last time, the great king breathed his last at midnight. In the morning the palace woke to the queens' cries of grief.
incidents.image: Rama leaving for fourteen years of exile from Ayodhya.jpg

incidents.title: Messengers Ride to Bharata
incidents.story: Since no son was near, Vasishtha had the king's body kept safe in oil. He sent swift messengers to the kingdom of Kekaya to bring Bharata home. They were told to carry gifts and not to reveal the sad news, but only to say that he was needed urgently.
incidents.image: The marriage of Bharata and Mandavi (6125129180).jpg

incidents.title: Bharata's Bad Dream
incidents.story: Far away in his grandfather's palace, Bharata had a terrible dream about his father. He woke troubled, and his friends tried in vain to cheer him with music and stories. That very day the messengers arrived, and Bharata hurried toward Ayodhya with his brother Shatrughna.
incidents.image: Bharata Carry Slippers of Rama to Ayodhya.jpg

incidents.title: Bharata Hurries Home
incidents.story: After a long journey, Bharata reached Ayodhya and found the city strangely silent and gloomy. There was no music, no joy in the streets. With a heavy heart he went to his mother's palace, hoping to see his father there.
incidents.image: Bharata comes to greet Rama, who is acclaimed by the people of Ayodhya.jpg

incidents.title: Bharata Rebukes Kaikeyi
incidents.story: Kaikeyi told Bharata that his father had died and that Rama had been sent to the forest so he could be king. Bharata was shocked and grief-stricken. He spoke angry words to his mother for causing such sorrow, and declared he would never take his brother's place.
incidents.image: Rama returns to Ayodhya.jpg

incidents.title: The Last Rites for Dasharatha
incidents.story: Guided by Vasishtha, Bharata performed his father's funeral with full honor. The body of the great king was carried to the banks of the Sarayu and given to the sacred fire. The queens and the people mourned the passing of a ruler who had loved them like a father.
incidents.image: Kekeyi informs Rama and Lakshmana of the decision of Dasharatha.jpg

incidents.title: Manthara and Shatrughna
incidents.story: When Shatrughna saw Manthara dressed in fine jewels, his anger flared and he seized her roughly. Bharata stopped him, saying that Rama would be displeased if they harmed a woman. Shatrughna let her go, and the frightened maid ran to Kaikeyi.
incidents.image: Birth of Bharata, Lakshmana, and Shatrughna, Folio from a Ramayana (Adventures of Rama) LACMA M.83.105.13.jpg

incidents.title: Bharata Refuses the Crown
incidents.story: The ministers and Vasishtha asked Bharata to become king. Bharata firmly refused, saying the throne belonged to Rama, the eldest. He ordered a road to be made through the forest and set out with the army, the queens and the people to bring Rama home.
incidents.image: Bharata and Shatrughana paying homage to Sage Bharadwaja at his hermitage.jpg

incidents.title: Guha's Doubt
incidents.story: When Guha saw Bharata's great army near the Ganga, he feared Bharata meant to harm Rama. But when they met, Bharata's sorrow and love were clear. Guha was moved and told him how Lakshmana had kept watch, and Bharata wept to see the grass bed where Rama had slept.
incidents.image: Birth of Bharata, Lakshmana, and Shatrughna, Folio from a Ramayana (Adventures of Rama) LACMA M.83.105.13.jpg

incidents.title: Bharadvaja's Wondrous Feast
incidents.story: At Prayaga, the sage Bharadvaja first tested Bharata's heart and was pleased by his devotion to Rama. Then, by the power of his penance, he called upon the gods to prepare a wondrous feast. The whole army enjoyed food, music and rest as if in heaven for one night.
incidents.image: Rama, Sita, and Lakshmana at the Hermitage of Bharadvaja Page from a dispersed Ramayana (Story of King Rama), ca. 1780.jpg

incidents.title: Lakshmana Sees the Army
incidents.story: At Chitrakuta, Rama noticed rising dust and frightened animals. Lakshmana climbed a tall tree and saw Bharata's army and its banner. Thinking Bharata had come to attack, he grew angry and readied his bow. Rama calmed him, saying Bharata had surely come out of love.
incidents.image: India, Datia - A page from a Ramayana- Rama, Lakshman and Sita before a slain giant - 2018.122 - Cleveland Museum of Art.jpg

incidents.title: Brothers Meet at Chitrakuta
incidents.story: Bharata saw Rama sitting outside his hut in bark clothes and matted hair, and ran to him weeping. He fell at Rama's feet, too overcome to speak. Rama lifted him up, embraced him lovingly, and asked about their father and the kingdom.
incidents.image: Vali dying.jpg

incidents.title: Offerings for Father
incidents.story: When Rama heard that Dasharatha had died, he fell to the ground in grief. With his brothers and Sita he went to the river Mandakini and offered water and simple forest food for their father's peace. The mothers came, and Kausalya wept to see such humble offerings.
incidents.image: Rama taking leave of Dasharatha.jpg
incidents.artist: Asian Art at the San Diego Museum of Art

incidents.title: Jabali's Argument
incidents.story: The learned Jabali tried to persuade Rama to return by arguing that duty to a dead father did not matter and only this life counts. Rama firmly answered that truth is the root of dharma. He would never break his word, and he gently rebuked Jabali's view.
incidents.image: Abd al-Rahim - The Ramayana (Tales of Rama; The Freer Ramayana) - Google Art Project.jpg
incidents.artist: Abd al-Rahim – Patron Details on Google Art Project

incidents.title: Vasishtha's Plea
incidents.story: Vasishtha told Rama the long history of the Ikshvaku kings, in which the eldest son always ruled. As Rama's teacher, he asked him to accept the throne. Rama bowed respectfully but said a father's command must be honored above all, so he would stay in the forest.
incidents.image: Clevelandart 2018.117.jpg

incidents.title: Bharata Sits at the Door
incidents.story: Bharata declared that he would sit before Rama's hut without food until Rama agreed to return. He spread grass on the ground and sat down. Rama gently told him this was not the way of a prince, and asked him to rise and go back to rule Ayodhya.
incidents.image: Bharata sets out to find Rama 1.jpg

incidents.title: The Sandals of Rama
incidents.story: When Rama would not return, Bharata asked him to step onto a pair of sandals. Rama did so and gave them to Bharata. Bharata placed them on his head and vowed to rule only in Rama's name for fourteen years, and to give up his life if Rama did not return on time.
incidents.image: Rama and Lakshmana receive Bharata and his companions.jpg

incidents.title: Kingdom of the Sandals
incidents.story: Bharata did not sit on the throne in Ayodhya. He went to the village of Nandigrama, wore bark and matted hair like Rama, and placed Rama's sandals on the throne. He ruled the kingdom humbly as their servant, waiting each day for his brother's return.
incidents.image: Rama Returns to Ayodhya.jpg
incidents.artist: Ramachandra Madhwa Mahishi, Illustrated by Balasaheb Pandit

incidents.title: Leaving Chitrakuta
incidents.story: After Bharata left, Chitrakuta held too many memories for Rama, and the hermits there were troubled by demons. So Rama, Sita and Lakshmana decided to move deeper into the forest. They bid farewell to their beloved hills and set out toward the south.
incidents.image: Bharata Shoots at Hanuman as He Flies Over with the Medicinal Herbs (recto), Hanuman Lands with the Medicinal Herbs (verso), Scenes from the Story of the Burning of Lanka, Folio from a LACMA M.85.297.5a-b (1 of 2).jpg

incidents.title: Anasuya's Gifts to Sita
incidents.story: At the hermitage of the sage Atri, his wife Anasuya, famous for her great penance, welcomed Sita like a daughter. She praised Sita's devotion to Rama and gave her a heavenly garland, clothes, jewels and an ointment that would never fade. Then Sita lovingly told her the story of her wedding.
incidents.image: Anonymous - Rama and Lakshmana Converse with Atri at His Ashram While Sita Talks to his Wife, Anasuya, from a Ramayana series - 1995.69 - Arthur M. Sackler Museum.jpg

incidents.title: Welcome to the Dandaka Forest
incidents.story: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana entered the vast Dandaka forest, where many hermitages stood among the trees. The sages living there came out joyfully to greet them with fruits, flowers and water. They told Rama that as their king he was their protector, and they gave him a humble home for the night.
incidents.image: Sita offering fruits to Rama in Dandaka forest.jpg

incidents.title: Viradha Seizes Sita
incidents.story: As the three walked deeper into the forest, a huge and terrible demon named Viradha rushed at them. He snatched Sita up in his arms and roared that he would keep her. Rama was filled with sorrow and anger, and Lakshmana blazed with fury, ready to fight to save her.
incidents.image: Destruction of Demon, Viradha, and ascent of Sage Sharabhanga to heaven, Kangra School of Art, circa 1780 CE, CSMVS, Mumbai.jpg

incidents.title: Viradha Freed From His Curse
incidents.story: Rama and Lakshmana struck Viradha with arrows, but a boon kept weapons from killing him. So the brothers broke his arms and buried him in a deep pit. As he died, Viradha revealed he was a gandharva named Tumburu, cursed long ago, and Rama's touch had finally set him free.
incidents.image: 1780 CE Rama and Sita in forest, Lakshmana removing thorn.jpg

incidents.title: Sharabhanga Rises to Heaven
incidents.story: Rama reached the hermitage of the sage Sharabhanga, where Indra himself had come to visit. The old sage had waited only to see Rama before leaving the world. After blessing Rama, Sharabhanga entered a sacred fire and rose from it shining and young, ascending to the world of Brahma.
incidents.image: Rama and SIta in Forest, Kangra Style 1780.jpg

incidents.title: The Bones of the Slain Sages
incidents.story: Many hermits gathered around Rama and showed him a sad sight: heaps of bones of holy men killed by cruel rakshasas in the forest. With folded hands they begged Rama to save them. Their suffering touched Rama's heart deeply and showed him why he had come to Dandaka.
incidents.image: Ravana, overwhelmed by grief on hearing of his son's deat, sends out more forces against Rama. From Mewar Ramayana.jpg

incidents.title: Rama's Vow to Protect the Sages
incidents.story: Rama gently told the hermits not to bow to him, for it was his duty to serve them. He promised to destroy the rakshasas who harmed them. This vow to protect the helpless became the purpose of his forest life and set in motion everything that followed.
incidents.image: Rama and SIta in Forest, Kangra Style 1780.jpg

incidents.title: Sita's Gentle Warning
incidents.story: As they walked on, Sita spoke softly to Rama. She worried that carrying weapons might lead him to harm creatures who had done no wrong, and told the tale of a sage who grew violent after keeping a sword. Rama praised her wisdom but explained he must keep his promise to protect the sages.
incidents.image: Rama, Sita, and Lakshmana, Folio from a Ramayana LACMA M.87.278.10.jpg

incidents.title: The Hermitage of Sutikshna
incidents.story: Rama visited the great sage Sutikshna, who had long been waiting for him. The sage welcomed the three warmly and offered them his hermitage as their home for as long as they wished. Rama stayed the night and then set out, promising to return after visiting the other forest sages.
incidents.image: Sita in the Forest Grove (left); Rama and Lakshmana Stricken (right), Folio from the "Shangri" Ramayana (Adventures of Rama) LACMA M.91.348.2.jpg

incidents.title: Ten Happy Years in the Forest
incidents.story: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana wandered from one hermitage to another, staying a few months here and a year there. They were welcomed everywhere with love. Ten peaceful years passed this way, and they learned much from the wise sages before returning to Sutikshna.
incidents.image: Rama, Sita and Lakshman approaching the hermitage of the sage Atri (6125136010).jpg

incidents.title: Agastya Defeats Vatapi
incidents.story: Near Agastya's home, Rama told Lakshmana an old tale. The demon Ilvala used to cook his brother Vatapi as food for guests, then call him back alive, killing them. When Agastya ate the meal, he digested Vatapi completely, and burned Ilvala with a glance. Rama also recalled how the Vindhya mountain bowed to Agastya's word.
incidents.image: Rama at the Hermatige of Sage Agastya.jpg
incidents.artist: Pahari School, Chamba kalam, Kangra idiom

incidents.title: Agastya's Divine Weapons
incidents.story: The great sage Agastya welcomed Rama with honor at his radiant hermitage. He gave Rama a mighty bow of Vishnu made by Vishwakarma, an arrow from Brahma, two quivers that never run out of arrows from Indra, and a golden sword. Then he advised Rama to make his home at Panchavati.
incidents.image: Killing of Rawana Painting by Balasaheb Pant Pratinidhi.jpg
incidents.artist: Balasaheb Pandit Pant Pratinidhi (author dead before 1952 (A

incidents.title: Meeting Jatayu
incidents.story: On the way to Panchavati, Rama met a giant, noble vulture named Jatayu. He said he had been a friend of King Dasharatha and offered to watch over Sita whenever the brothers went away. Rama embraced him warmly, happy to find an old friend of his father in the forest.
incidents.image: Anonymous - Rama and Lakshmana Discover the Dying Jatayu, from a Ramayana series - 1995.70 - Arthur M. Sackler Museum.jpg

incidents.title: The Hut at Panchavati
incidents.story: At Panchavati, near the Godavari river, Lakshmana built a lovely hut of mud, bamboo and leaves. Rama was so moved by his brother's loving work that he embraced him with tears of joy. There the three lived happily for a time, surrounded by flowers, birds and deer.
incidents.image: At Panchavati - Lakshmana preparing food and Sita making a garland of flowers.jpg

incidents.title: Winter by the Godavari
incidents.story: One cold winter morning, the brothers walked to the river to bathe. Lakshmana described the frosty fields and misty sun, then thought of Bharata, who lived like a hermit in Ayodhya and bathed in the icy Sarayu out of love for Rama. Rama too longed for his gentle brother.
incidents.image: Popular print, album (BM 2003,1022,0.75).jpg
incidents.artist: Printed by: Ravi Varma Press After: Raja Ravi Varma

incidents.title: Shurpanakha Comes to Panchavati
incidents.story: A rakshasi named Shurpanakha, Ravana's sister, saw Rama and wished to marry him. Rama said he was already married and jokingly sent her to Lakshmana, who sent her back. Angry and jealous, she rushed at Sita, meaning to harm her, and Rama quickly stopped her.
incidents.image: Clevelandart 2018.107.jpg

incidents.title: Shurpanakha Is Punished
incidents.story: To protect Sita, Rama told Lakshmana to punish the rakshasi. Lakshmana drew his sword and cut off Shurpanakha's nose and ears. Screaming with pain and rage, she fled through the forest to her brother Khara, and this moment began a great chain of events.
incidents.image: Rama and Lakshmana Search in Vain for Sita (IA mma rama and lakshmana search in vain for sita 37910).jpg

incidents.title: Khara's Fourteen Warriors
incidents.story: Shurpanakha told Khara what had happened, and he sent fourteen fierce rakshasas to kill the brothers. Rama asked Lakshmana to guard Sita and faced them alone. With fourteen golden arrows he struck them all down, and Shurpanakha ran back to Khara in fear.
incidents.image: Delhi-National Museum-Rama piercing the Ravana's neck with his arrows-20131006.jpg
incidents.artist: Miniature of the Muhammad Shah period Shangri , école d’art

incidents.title: The Army of Khara and Dushana
incidents.story: Furious, Khara marched out with Dushana, Trishiras and an army of fourteen thousand rakshasas. Dark omens filled the sky as they came. Rama calmly sent Lakshmana to take Sita to a safe cave, then put on his armor and waited, shining like a fire.
incidents.image: Rama and Lakshmana Search in Vain for Sita.jpg

incidents.title: Rama Stands Alone
incidents.story: Gods and sages gathered in the sky to watch as Rama faced the huge army by himself. His arrows flew so fast that no one could see him draw the bow. In a short time the great army lay defeated, and the fierce general Dushana fell to his arrows too.
incidents.image: Delhi-National Museum-Rama piercing the Ravana's neck with his arrows-20131006.jpg
incidents.artist: Miniature of the Muhammad Shah period Shangri , école d’art

incidents.title: The Fall of Trishiras
incidents.story: The three-headed warrior Trishiras charged at Rama, boasting that he would win. He struck Rama's forehead with arrows, but Rama stood firm. Then Rama shot down his horses and charioteer and cut off all three of his heads, leaving Khara alone on the battlefield.
incidents.image: Ascent of Rama, From the Mewar Ramayana.jpg

incidents.title: The End of Khara
incidents.story: Khara fought Rama in a fierce duel, breaking his armor and hurling a great tree at him. At last Rama struck him with the shining arrow of Indra that Agastya had given him, and Khara fell. The sages rejoiced, and Sita joyfully embraced her victorious husband.
incidents.image: Rama's forest dwelling in Panchavati.jpg

incidents.title: Akampana Brings the News
incidents.story: A rakshasa named Akampana escaped the battle and flew to Lanka. He told Ravana that Rama had destroyed Khara and his whole army. He said no one could defeat Rama in battle, but suggested that Ravana carry away Sita, for Rama could not live without her.
incidents.image: Ascent of Rama, From the Mewar Ramayana.jpg

incidents.title: Maricha's First Counsel
incidents.story: Ravana went to the rakshasa Maricha to ask for help in taking Sita. Maricha warned him that whoever gave this advice was an enemy, and that Rama was too mighty to anger. He urged Ravana to go home and live peacefully. Ravana listened and returned to Lanka.
incidents.image: Events at Panchavati forest.jpg

incidents.title: Shurpanakha Goads Ravana
incidents.story: Shurpanakha arrived in Lanka and scolded Ravana in front of his court for being a careless king while his people were slain. She told him how Rama had killed Khara's army and praised Sita's beauty. Her words stirred Ravana's pride and desire, and he made up his mind.
incidents.image: Ravana comes in disguise with a begging bowl to abduct Sita.jpg

incidents.title: Maricha's Second Warning
incidents.story: Ravana flew across the sea again to Maricha, now living as a hermit. Maricha remembered how Rama's arrow had once hurled him far into the ocean at Vishvamitra's sacrifice. He begged Ravana to stop, but when Ravana threatened to kill him, Maricha sadly agreed to help.
incidents.image: Kkmenonmarichanpainting.png

incidents.title: The Golden Deer
incidents.story: Maricha became a wondrous deer, golden with silver spots and jewel-like horns, and wandered near the hut. Sita was delighted and longed to have it. Lakshmana warned it must be Maricha in disguise, but Rama, wishing to please Sita, went after it and told Lakshmana to guard her carefully.
incidents.image: The Demon Marichi Tries to Dissuade Ravana (IA mma the demon marichi tries to dissuade ravana 37954).jpg

incidents.title: Maricha's False Cry
incidents.story: The deer led Rama far into the forest, appearing and vanishing again and again. At last Rama shot it with an arrow. As he died, Maricha took his own form and cried out in Rama's voice, calling for Sita and Lakshmana, to trick them. Rama felt a chill of worry and hurried back.
incidents.image: Rama stalks the demon Maricha, who has assumed the form of a golden deer.jpg

incidents.title: Sita's Harsh Words
incidents.story: Hearing the cry, Sita begged Lakshmana to go to Rama's aid. Lakshmana gently said no one could harm Rama, and he would not leave her. In her fear, Sita spoke cruel and unfair words against him. Deeply hurt, Lakshmana bowed, asked the forest spirits to guard her, and left.
incidents.image: Popular print, album (BM 2003,1022,0.75 1).jpg
incidents.artist: Printed by: Ravi Varma Press After: Raja Ravi Varma

incidents.title: Ravana Comes as a Mendicant
incidents.story: As soon as Sita was alone, Ravana appeared dressed as a holy wandering monk, with a staff and water pot. The trees grew still and the Godavari slowed in fear. Sita, thinking him a sage, welcomed him kindly as a guest and offered him a seat and food.
incidents.image: Unknown (Indian) - Sita Imprisoned at Ravana's Palace, Ravana Holding Court (Illustration to the Ramayana) - 70.729 - Detroit Institute of Arts.jpg

incidents.title: Sita's Fearless Reply
incidents.story: Ravana revealed who he was and asked Sita to become his queen. Sita stood firm and answered bravely. She said Rama was like a lion and Ravana like a jackal, and that he could never win her. Her loyalty to Rama shone brighter than all of Ravana's boasting.
incidents.image: Rama During his Search of Sita Meets Wounded Jatayu and Comes to Know that Ravana Abducted Sita - late 18th-century.jpg

incidents.title: The Abduction of Sita
incidents.story: Ravana took on his true, fearsome form and seized Sita. He carried her into his flying chariot and rose into the sky. Weeping, Sita called out to Rama and Lakshmana, and asked the trees, the river and the animals to tell Rama what had happened to her.
incidents.image: Rama and Lakshmana bound - Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda (1652), f.34 - BL Add MS 15297.jpg

incidents.title: Jatayu's Brave Fight
incidents.story: The old vulture Jatayu heard Sita's cries and flew at Ravana to stop him. Though very old, he broke Ravana's bow, killed his donkeys and charioteer, and smashed the chariot. At last Ravana cut off Jatayu's wings and feet with his sword, and the brave bird fell to the ground.
incidents.image: Jatayu Attacks Ravana to Save Sita and Shatters his Chariot - early 18th-century.jpg

incidents.title: Ornaments Dropped to the Monkeys
incidents.story: As Ravana flew south with her, Sita saw five monkeys sitting on a mountain top. She tied her jewels in a piece of her silk scarf and dropped it among them, hoping they would tell Rama. Ravana did not notice, and this clever act later helped Rama find her.
incidents.image: Ravi Varma-Ravana Sita Jathayu.jpg

incidents.title: Sita Refuses Ravana in Lanka
incidents.story: In Lanka, Ravana showed Sita his golden palace and treasures and begged her to be his queen. Sita placed a blade of grass between them and refused him, saying she belonged only to Rama. Angry, Ravana gave her twelve months to change her mind and kept her in the Ashoka grove.
incidents.image: Ravana seizes Sita by the hair to abduct her to Lanka.jpg

incidents.title: Rama's Grief and Search
incidents.story: Rama returned to find the hut empty and Sita gone. Overcome by sorrow, he searched everywhere, asking the trees, rivers and animals if they had seen her. The deer looked toward the south, and the brothers found flowers, broken weapons and a shattered chariot along the way.
incidents.image: Sita complled by Rama to undrego the ordeal of fire.jpg

incidents.title: Jatayu's Last Words
incidents.story: Rama found Jatayu lying wounded and dying. The faithful bird told him that Ravana had carried Sita away to the south, and then breathed his last. Rama wept for him as for his own father and performed his funeral rites with love, and Jatayu rose to the higher worlds.
incidents.image: Raja Ravi Varma, Jatayu vadha, 1906.jpg

incidents.title: Ayomukhi in the Dark Forest
incidents.story: Searching for Sita, the brothers entered a thick, gloomy forest. There a fearsome rakshasi named Ayomukhi seized Lakshmana and wanted him for her husband. Lakshmana drew his sword, cut off her nose and ears, and she ran away, leaving the brothers to continue their search.
incidents.image: Rama with sita and Lakshman (detail).jpg

incidents.title: Kabandha's Advice
incidents.story: A strange giant named Kabandha, with no head and very long arms, caught the brothers. They cut off his arms, and he told them he was a cursed gandharva. After they cremated him, he rose in shining form and advised Rama to make friends with the monkey king Sugriva, who would help find Sita.
incidents.image: Killing of Kabandha.jpg

incidents.title: Shabari's Hermitage
incidents.story: Following Kabandha's directions, Rama and Lakshmana reached the hermitage of Shabari, a holy woman who had served the sages of Matanga. She welcomed them with forest fruits and showed them the sacred grove. Her wait fulfilled, she entered a fire and rose to heaven. In later tellings, she tasted each berry to offer Rama only the sweet ones.
incidents.image: Indischer Maler von 1780 001.jpg

incidents.title: Arrival at Pampa Lake
incidents.story: At last the brothers came to the beautiful Pampa lake, full of lotuses, birds and clear water. Nearby rose the Rishyamuka mountain, where Sugriva lived. Though Rama still grieved for Sita, his heart filled with new hope that friends and help were near.
incidents.image: Rama and Lakshmana arrive at Lake Pampa, From the Mewar Ramayana.jpg

incidents.title: Rama's Longing at Pampa
incidents.story: Rama and Lakshmana reached the lovely lake Pampa in spring. Lotuses bloomed, bees hummed and birds sang, but every sweet sight made Rama miss Sita even more. Lakshmana gently reminded his brother to be brave and hopeful, for courage, not sorrow, would help them find her.
incidents.image: 1653 CE Ramayana manuscript, Mewar manuscript, Kiskindha kanda, Rama and Lakshmana arrive at Lake Pampa (now Hampi, Vijayanagara), Hanuman finds them.jpg

incidents.title: Sugriva Fears the Two Archers
incidents.story: On Rishyamuka hill, the monkey prince Sugriva saw two strong archers walking by the lake. He trembled, thinking his brother Vali had sent them to kill him. His wise minister Hanuman calmed him and agreed to go down and learn who these strangers really were.
incidents.image: Sugriva challenge Vali recto.jpg

incidents.title: Hanuman Comes as a Mendicant
incidents.story: Hanuman hid his monkey form and appeared before Rama and Lakshmana as a humble wandering ascetic. With great politeness he praised their noble looks and asked who they were. He then told them about Sugriva, the exiled monkey king who wished to be their friend.
incidents.image: Rama and Lakshman in the howdah of an white elephant with Hanuman as mahout (6125101262).jpg

incidents.title: Rama Praises Hanuman's Speech
incidents.story: Rama was delighted by Hanuman's words. He told Lakshmana that no one could speak so clearly and sweetly without knowing the Vedas well. Not one word was wrong or out of place. This was how Rama first saw the wisdom of the devotee who would serve him forever.
incidents.image: Hanuman's monkey army, Rama and Lakshman in front of the castle in Lanka (6125072936).jpg

incidents.title: Hanuman Carries the Princes
incidents.story: Hanuman took back his true form and joyfully lifted Rama and Lakshmana onto his shoulders. He leapt across the hills to bring them to Sugriva. Lakshmana told Hanuman their sad story, and Hanuman promised that Sugriva would help them search for Sita.
incidents.image: Rama and Lakshman in the howdah of an white elephant with Hanuman as mahout (6125101262).jpg

incidents.title: Friendship Sworn Before Fire
incidents.story: Hanuman lit a sacred fire with two sticks. Rama and Sugriva walked around it together, clasped hands and promised to be true friends. Each vowed to share the other's joys and sorrows. This friendship, made before Agni, would change the fate of both.
incidents.image: Lakshmana Meets with Tara, Sugriva, and Hanuman in the Palace of Kishkandha, Folio from a Ramayana (Adventures of Rama) LACMA M.73.50.jpg

incidents.title: Sita's Ornaments Shown
incidents.story: Sugriva said his monkeys once saw a weeping lady carried through the sky, who dropped a bundle of jewels. He brought it, and Rama held Sita's ornaments to his heart and wept. Lakshmana said he knew only her anklets, because he had bowed at her feet each day.
incidents.image: Brooklyn Museum - Rama and Lakshmana Confer with Sugriva about the Search for Sita Page from a Dispersed Ramayana Series.jpg

incidents.title: Vali and the Demon Mayavi
incidents.story: Sugriva told how the demon Mayavi once challenged Vali at night. The brothers chased him to a deep cave, and Vali went in, asking Sugriva to wait. After a long year, blood flowed out and no sound of Vali came. Thinking him dead, Sugriva sadly closed the cave with a rock.
incidents.image: Lakshmana Meets with Tara, Sugriva, and Hanuman in the Palace of Kishkandha, Folio from a Ramayana (Adventures of Rama) LACMA M.73.50.jpg

incidents.title: Sugriva Is Cast Out
incidents.story: The monkeys made Sugriva king, but Vali came home alive and furious. He believed Sugriva had trapped him on purpose to steal the throne. Vali drove his brother away and took Sugriva's wife Ruma. Sugriva fled to Rishyamuka, where a sage's curse kept Vali from coming.
incidents.image: Brooklyn Museum - Rama and Lakshmana Confer with Sugriva about the Search for Sita Page from a Dispersed Ramayana Series.jpg

incidents.title: Dundubhi's Skeleton Kicked
incidents.story: Sugriva showed Rama the huge, dried skeleton of Dundubhi, a buffalo demon Vali had once killed and flung far away. To test Rama's strength, Sugriva asked him to move it. Rama simply flicked it with his toe, and the mountain of bones flew a great distance.
incidents.image: Tara with Her Son Angad Receiving an Angry Lakshmana at the Gates of Kishkindha - c. 1820s.jpg

incidents.title: Seven Sala Trees Pierced
incidents.story: Sugriva said the bones were dry and light, so Rama showed more. He shot one arrow that passed through seven giant sala trees, through a hill and into the earth, and then returned to his quiver. Sugriva bowed in wonder, sure now that Rama could defeat Vali.
incidents.image: "Rama Receives Sugriva and Jambavat, the Monkey and Bear Kings", Folio from a Ramayana MET DP107190.jpg

incidents.title: The First Duel
incidents.story: Sugriva roared at the gates of Kishkindha, and Vali rushed out to fight. The two brothers looked so alike that Rama, hidden nearby, could not tell them apart and held back his arrow. Bruised and beaten, Sugriva fled, and Rama explained he had feared harming his own friend.
incidents.image: Tara with Her Son Angad Receiving an Angry Lakshmana at the Gates of Kishkindha - c. 1820s.jpg

incidents.title: The Garland of Flowers
incidents.story: So that Rama could know his friend in battle, Lakshmana placed a garland of blooming flowers around Sugriva's neck. Shining with the bright creeper, Sugriva went back to Kishkindha full of new hope, trusting Rama's promise to help him this time.
incidents.image: Sugriva leads Rama and Lakshman to Kishkindha, the capital of Bali (6124520455).jpg

incidents.title: Tara Warns Vali
incidents.story: When Sugriva roared again, Vali's wise queen Tara stopped him. She had heard that Sugriva had made friends with the mighty Rama, and begged Vali to make peace with his brother. Proud Vali would not listen. He said Rama was righteous and would do no wrong, and went out to fight.
incidents.image: Sugriva roars out his challenge to his usurping brother Bali.jpg

incidents.title: The Second Duel
incidents.story: Vali and Sugriva clashed like two mountains, striking with fists, trees and rocks. Slowly Vali grew stronger and Sugriva began to tire. Sugriva looked around for help, hoping his friend Rama was watching and keeping his word.
incidents.image: Sugriva leads Rama and Lakshman to Kishkindha, the capital of Bali (6124520455).jpg

incidents.title: Vali Is Struck Down
incidents.story: Seeing Sugriva weaken, Rama fitted a mighty arrow to his bow and let it fly. It struck Vali in the chest, and the great monkey king fell to the ground like a tall tree. Even as he lay there, the golden necklace given by Indra still shone on him.
incidents.image: Death of Valin, King of the Monkeys, 1975-148-3.jpg

incidents.title: Vali's Reproach and Rama's Answer
incidents.story: Wounded Vali blamed Rama for striking him while he fought another. Rama answered calmly that the land was ruled by Bharata, and that Vali had taken his younger brother's wife, a grave wrong. A king must punish such deeds. Vali accepted this and asked Rama's forgiveness.
incidents.image: Rama Kills Vali, Folio from the 'Impey' Ramayana (Adventures of Rama) LACMA M.72.88.3.jpg

incidents.title: Vali's Last Request
incidents.story: As his life faded, Vali asked Rama and Sugriva to care for his son Angada. He told Sugriva to trust Tara's wise counsel, and gave him his shining golden necklace. He advised Angada to serve his uncle faithfully. Brothers who had quarreled parted in peace.
incidents.image: Rama Chastises the Dying Vali, Folio from a Ramayana (Adventures of Rama) LACMA M.82.6.5.jpg

incidents.title: Tara's Lament
incidents.story: Tara ran to the battlefield and embraced fallen Vali, weeping for her husband. She grieved that Angada had lost his father. Hanuman gently comforted her, and Sugriva too was filled with sorrow and regret. Rama spoke kindly to Tara and eased her pain.
incidents.image: Tara, by Raja Ravi Varma.jpg

incidents.title: The Funeral of Vali
incidents.story: The monkeys carried Vali on a grand bier decorated with flowers to a riverbank. With tears in his eyes, young Angada lit his father's funeral fire. Sugriva and all the monkeys offered water for Vali's soul, honoring their brave king.
incidents.image: Nainsukh - The Monkey King Vali's Funeral Pyre, Illustrated folio from a dispersed Ramayana series - 2004.367 - Metropolitan Museum of Art.jpg

incidents.title: Sugriva Crowned King
incidents.story: Sugriva was crowned king of Kishkindha, and Angada was made crown prince. Rama did not enter the city, keeping his vow to live in the forest. He told Sugriva to enjoy the rainy season and begin the search for Sita when the rains ended.
incidents.image: Hanuman, sugriva and jambvan.jpg

incidents.title: Rama's Grief in the Rains
incidents.story: Rama and Lakshmana stayed in a cave on Prasravana hill through the monsoon. Dark clouds rolled, rivers swelled, and peacocks danced, but Rama could not sleep for missing Sita. Lakshmana stayed beside him, comforting him and reminding him that autumn would bring their chance to act.
incidents.image: Rama and Lakshman converse with a man at night, while the others sleep (6125095504).jpg

incidents.title: Sugriva Forgets His Promise
incidents.story: Happy in his palace, Sugriva spent his days in comfort and forgot his duty to Rama. Wise Hanuman reminded him of his promise, and Sugriva sent for his armies. Yet when autumn arrived, Rama saw no sign of help and sent Lakshmana to Kishkindha.
incidents.image: Folio from a Ramayana manuscript, text in Devanagari.jpg

incidents.title: Lakshmana's Anger
incidents.story: Lakshmana strode into Kishkindha with his bow, burning with anger at Sugriva's delay. The monkeys trembled as he twanged his bowstring with a sound like thunder. Sugriva realized his mistake and was filled with fear and shame.
incidents.image: Lakshmana and the monkey king Sugriva are conversing in a palanquin carried by four monkeys to offer allegiance to Rama..jpg

incidents.title: Tara Calms Lakshmana
incidents.story: Sugriva sent wise Tara to meet Lakshmana. With gentle words she asked him to forgive Sugriva and explained that armies were already being called from every land. Lakshmana's anger cooled, and Sugriva humbly came out, promising to serve Rama with all his heart.
incidents.image: Rama and Lakshmana Meet Sugriva at Matanga’s Hermitage.jpg

incidents.title: The Monkey Armies Gather
incidents.story: Millions of monkeys and bears poured into Kishkindha from mountains, forests and seashores. Great leaders like Jambavan, Nila and Sushena brought their troops. The ground shook beneath them. Rama was overjoyed to see such a mighty army ready to search for Sita.
incidents.image: Rama’s allies, from the left, all standing in profile, Sugriva, king of the vanaras, followed by Angada and Jambavan, king of the bears..jpg

incidents.title: Sugriva Describes the Four Directions
incidents.story: Sugriva sent search parties east, west, north and south. He described each land in detail, its rivers, mountains and peoples, so the monkeys knew where to look. He gave them one month to return with news, and sent his best heroes, Angada, Hanuman and Jambavan, south.
incidents.image: "Rama Receives Sugriva and Jambavat, the Monkey and Bear Kings", Folio from a Ramayana MET DP103079.jpg

incidents.title: Rama Gives Hanuman His Ring
incidents.story: Rama felt sure that Hanuman would find Sita. He gave Hanuman his ring, carved with his own name, so that Sita would trust him as Rama's true messenger. Hanuman bowed, held the ring with great care, and set out on the search.
incidents.image: Rama and Sita enthroned in a pavilion, attended by Hanuman (6125134066).jpg

incidents.title: Swayamprabha's Hidden Cave
incidents.story: Searching the dry southern lands, thirsty monkeys entered a dark cave and found a golden city full of fruit and water. There the holy woman Swayamprabha fed them. She asked them to close their eyes, and by her power they found themselves beside the great ocean.
incidents.image: "Rama Receives Sugriva and Jambavat, the Monkey and Bear Kings", Folio from a Ramayana MET sf2002-503-a.jpg

incidents.title: Despair and Angada's Fast
incidents.story: The month had passed and Sita was still not found. Fearing Sugriva's anger, Angada decided to sit by the sea and fast until death, and the other monkeys joined him. As they grieved, they spoke of brave Jatayu, who died trying to save Sita.
incidents.image: Painting of Raja Jagat Prakash of Sirmur State worshipping Rama and Sita, ca.1790.jpg

incidents.title: Sampati and His Story
incidents.story: An old wingless vulture named Sampati heard the monkeys speak of Jatayu, his younger brother. He sadly asked how Jatayu had died. Then he told how, long ago, the two brothers flew toward the sun, and Sampati spread his wings to shield Jatayu, until his own wings burned.
incidents.image: Hanuman with Jambavan and Angada Meet Sampati, the Elder Brother of Jatayu - 1700-1800.jpg

incidents.title: Sampati Sees Sita in Lanka
incidents.story: With his sharp eagle eyes, Sampati looked far across the sea. He told the monkeys that Ravana had taken Sita to Lanka, a hundred yojanas away, where she sat sad among demons. As he helped Rama's cause, new wings grew on him, just as a sage had foretold.
incidents.image: The alliance between Rāma and Sugriva before Lanka.jpg

incidents.title: The Monkeys Measure Their Leaps
incidents.story: The monkeys gazed at the huge ocean and each said how far he could jump. Some could leap ten yojanas, some fifty, some ninety. Angada could reach a hundred but feared he could not return. No one was sure, and they fell silent with worry.
incidents.image: Angada smites the demon Narantaka.jpg

incidents.title: Jambavan Reminds Hanuman
incidents.story: Old Jambavan turned to Hanuman, who sat quietly. He reminded him that he was the son of the Wind God, that as a child he had leapt toward the sun thinking it a fruit, and that the gods had blessed him with great gifts. Hanuman began to feel his true strength.
incidents.image: At Jambavan's urging, Hanuman goes to the Himalayas to find the four healing plants 1.jpg

incidents.title: Hanuman Grows on Mahendra
incidents.story: Filled with faith in Rama, Hanuman grew huge and mighty, and the monkeys cheered. He climbed Mount Mahendra, which trembled under his feet. Gathering his strength and fixing his mind on Lanka, Hanuman got ready for the great leap across the ocean.
incidents.image: Hanuman carrying Rama on his shoulders.jpg

incidents.title: The Great Leap From Mahendra
incidents.story: Hanuman climbed Mount Mahendra and grew as large as a mountain. He bowed to the gods and to his father, the Wind, then pressed down with his feet and sprang into the sky. Trees flew up behind him as he soared south over the ocean toward Lanka, carrying everyone's hope of finding Sita.
incidents.image: Hanuman returns with sanjeevani mountain for laxmana's life.jpg

incidents.title: Mainaka Rises From the Sea
incidents.story: The Ocean remembered that Rama's ancestors, the sons of Sagara, had made it great, so it asked the golden mountain Mainaka to rise and give Hanuman a place to rest. Hanuman gently touched the mountain with his hand to honor its kindness. Then he flew on, refusing to pause until his task was done.
incidents.image: Zayn al'-'Abidin - Ramayana of Valmiki, vol. 2, folio 236, recto - Google Art Project.jpg
incidents.artist: Shyam Sundar Yusuf 'Ali Zayn al'-'Abidin Ghulam 'Ali

incidents.title: Surasa Tests Hanuman
incidents.story: The gods sent Surasa, mother of the serpents, to test Hanuman's strength and wisdom. She blocked his way and opened her huge mouth to swallow him. As she grew wider, he suddenly became as small as a thumb, darted in and out of her mouth, and bowed to her. Pleased, Surasa blessed him on his way.
incidents.image: Hanuman and Surasa.jpg

incidents.title: Simhika the Shadow-Seizer
incidents.story: Deep in the sea lived Simhika, a demoness who caught flying creatures by grabbing their shadows. Hanuman felt himself dragged down and saw her gaping jaws. He made himself tiny, slipped inside her, tore her apart, and burst out into the sky again. The heavenly beings praised his courage and quick thinking.
incidents.image: Monkeys and Bears fighting in the Madhuvana-Grove.jpg

incidents.title: Landing Before Lanka
incidents.story: Hanuman landed on a hill of Mount Trikuta, not even tired after crossing the ocean. Before him shone Lanka, a golden city with high walls, deep moats, and fierce guards. He waited until dusk, then shrank to the size of a cat so he could slip into the city unseen.
incidents.image: Hanuman Encounters Sita in Ashokavana.jpg

incidents.title: Lankini Guards the Gate
incidents.story: At the gate stood Lankini, the spirit who guarded the city. She shouted at Hanuman and struck him. He struck back lightly with his left fist, and she fell. Lankini then remembered Brahma's words: when a monkey defeats her, Lanka's end is near. She let Hanuman enter.
incidents.image: Monkeys plunder the Honey Grove on Hanuman's return from Lanka..jpg

incidents.title: Searching Lanka by Moonlight
incidents.story: Under a bright moon, Hanuman moved silently from house to house and palace to palace. He heard music and laughter and saw warriors, scholars, and rich halls everywhere. But in all that splendor he could not find Sita, and he kept searching with a patient and careful heart.
incidents.image: Sita, who is guarded by rakshasis at Lanka, looks at the ring given to her by Hanuman.jpg

incidents.title: The Pushpaka Chariot
incidents.story: In the heart of Ravana's palace, Hanuman saw the Pushpaka, a wondrous flying chariot that Ravana had taken from his brother Kubera. It glittered with gold and jewels and looked like a piece of heaven. Hanuman marveled at its beauty, but he did not forget the reason he had come.
incidents.image: Monkeys plunder the Honey Grove on Hanuman's return from Lanka..jpg

incidents.title: Ravana's Sleeping Chamber
incidents.story: Hanuman entered Ravana's own chamber, lit by golden lamps. The mighty king lay asleep on a splendid bed, breathing like a great serpent, while many queens slept around him. Hanuman looked carefully at each face, hoping and fearing that he might find Sita among them.
incidents.image: Rama and Hanuman fighting Ravana, an album painting on paper, c1820.jpg

incidents.title: Mistaking Mandodari for Sita
incidents.story: On a beautiful couch lay a queen of shining beauty, and Hanuman's heart leapt, thinking she must be Sita. He was so happy he jumped about like a monkey. But it was Mandodari, Ravana's chief queen. Soon he understood that Sita, parted from Rama, would never sleep peacefully in jewels.
incidents.image: Mandodari based on Raja Ravi Varma's painting.jpg

incidents.title: Hanuman's Self-Reproach
incidents.story: Hanuman worried that looking at sleeping women was wrong, but he knew his mind stayed pure because he searched only for Sita. Still finding nothing, he felt deep sorrow and feared he had failed Rama. Then he gathered his courage, prayed to Rama and Sita, and decided to search on.
incidents.image: Hanumans finds Sita in Ashokavana.jpg

incidents.title: Entering the Ashoka Grove
incidents.story: Hanuman leapt over a wall into the Ashoka grove, a lovely garden full of flowering trees, ponds, and singing birds. He climbed a tall shimshupa tree with thick leaves, where he could watch without being seen. He hoped that Sita, who loved forests, might be found in this quiet place.
incidents.image: Sita in Ashoka Vatika.jpg

incidents.title: First Sight of Sita
incidents.story: Beneath the tree sat a lady in a single worn garment, thin from fasting and pale with grief, like the moon behind clouds. Fierce demon women guarded her all around. Hanuman knew at once that this was Sita, and tears of joy and sorrow filled his eyes.
incidents.image: Sita kidnap by Ravana.jpg

incidents.title: Ravana's Visit and Threat
incidents.story: As night ended, Ravana came to the grove with his queens, bright with jewels. He tried to win Sita with sweet words and promises of great riches. When she would not listen, he grew angry and gave her two months to accept him, or else he would have her killed.
incidents.image: Sita Shies Away from Hanuman, Believing He is Ravana in Disguise, Ramayana, 1594, The David Collection, Copenhagen.jpg

incidents.title: Sita's Blade of Grass
incidents.story: Sita would not even speak to Ravana directly. She placed a blade of grass between them and spoke to it instead. She told him to return her to Rama and warned that Rama's arrows would destroy him. Her courage and faithfulness shone like a lamp in the dark.
incidents.image: Ramayana(Burmese version).png

incidents.title: The Guards' Threats
incidents.story: After Ravana left, the demon women crowded around Sita. They shouted, waved weapons, and threatened to eat her if she did not agree to marry Ravana. Sita wept and trembled, but she would not give up her love for Rama, even when she felt completely alone.
incidents.image: “Sita Shies Away from Hanuman, Believing He is Ravana in Disguise”.jpg

incidents.title: Trijata's Dream
incidents.story: Trijata, a wise old demon woman, woke from sleep and told the others about her dream. She had seen Rama and Lakshmana dressed in white, shining with victory, and Ravana heading south in ruin while Lanka sank. She warned the guards to stop troubling Sita and ask her forgiveness instead.
incidents.image: Sri Rama with four.jpg

incidents.title: Sita's Despair
incidents.story: Alone and heartbroken, Sita felt she could not bear any more. She held the branch of the tree and thought of ending her life with her long braid. Just then good omens came to her: her left eye and arm began to throb, signs that happy news was near.
incidents.image: “Sita Shies Away from Hanuman, Believing He is Ravana in Disguise”.jpg

incidents.title: Hanuman Sings Rama's Story
