incidents.story: From high in the tree, Hanuman began to speak softly in sweet words. He told the story of King Dasharatha, of Rama's exile, of Sita being taken, and of Rama's search with his monkey friends. Sita looked up in wonder, hearing her beloved's story in that faraway land.
incidents.image: Hanuman before Rama.jpg

incidents.title: Sita's Doubt and Questions
incidents.story: Seeing a monkey in the tree, Sita was afraid that it might be Ravana in disguise, trying to trick her. Hanuman bowed low and spoke humbly. When she asked how he knew Rama, he described Rama's form, his noble qualities, and the friendship with Sugriva, until her heart began to trust him.
incidents.image: Hanuman allowing himself to be taken before Ravana.jpg

incidents.title: Rama's Ring
incidents.story: Hanuman gave Sita the ring that Rama had sent, marked with Rama's own name. Sita held it close, and her face lit up with joy, as if she had met Rama himself. She asked eagerly about Rama and Lakshmana, and Hanuman promised that Rama would soon come for her.
incidents.image: Rama and Sita enthroned with Hanuman and six devotees (6125064154).jpg

incidents.title: Hanuman Offers to Carry Sita
incidents.story: Hanuman offered to carry Sita on his back across the ocean to Rama at once. When she doubted his size, he grew as huge as a mountain. Sita gently refused. She feared falling in battle, would not willingly touch anyone but Rama, and wished Rama himself to win her back with honor.
incidents.image: Rama and Sita enthroned, adored by Hanuman; Lakshmana holds a morchal (6125082400).jpg

incidents.title: The Story of the Crow
incidents.story: As a secret sign for Rama, Sita told a story only the two of them knew. Once at Chitrakuta, a crow kept pecking at her. Rama sent a blade of grass after it, charged with mighty power. The crow fled everywhere but found no shelter, until it surrendered to Rama and lost one eye.
incidents.image: Rama, Lakshmana, and Sita take up residence at the foot of the bounteous Chitrakuta Mountain.jpg

incidents.title: The Hair Jewel
incidents.story: Sita untied a precious jewel she wore in her hair and gave it to Hanuman. She asked him to give it to Rama and say that she could hold on for only one more month. Hanuman bowed, circled her with respect, and comforted her before he left.
incidents.image: Rama and Sita Enthroned (6124522461).jpg

incidents.title: Destroying the Ashoka Grove
incidents.story: Before leaving, Hanuman wanted to test Ravana's strength and show Lanka the power of Rama's messengers. He tore up trees, broke pavilions, and smashed ponds, leaving the lovely garden in ruins. Only the tree where Sita sat was left untouched. The frightened guards ran to tell Ravana.
incidents.image: Hanuman's visit to Lanka.jpg

incidents.title: The Kinkaras Fall
incidents.story: Ravana angrily sent thousands of Kinkaras, his fierce servant warriors, to seize the monkey. Hanuman grew large, roared Rama's victory, and picked up an iron bar from the gateway. With it he struck down the whole army, showing that one faithful servant of Rama could stand against many.
incidents.image: Rama and Sita Enthroned (6124522461).jpg

incidents.title: Jambumali Is Defeated
incidents.story: Next came Jambumali, the strong son of the general Prahasta, riding a chariot and shooting sharp arrows. Hanuman was wounded but did not stop. He hurled a great iron bar that smashed Jambumali and his chariot. Lanka began to fear this single monkey.
incidents.image: Sree Raghunandan - Ram Laxman Sita and Hanuman, M V Dhurandar.jpg

incidents.title: The Ministers' Sons
incidents.story: Ravana sent seven brave sons of his ministers, each shining in armor on a grand chariot. They showered arrows on Hanuman like rain on a mountain. Hanuman leapt into the sky, roared, and struck them down one by one. Their families in Lanka wept, and Ravana grew worried.
incidents.image: Hanuman meets Ravana.jpg

incidents.title: The Five Generals
incidents.story: Ravana then sent five of his greatest commanders with their armies. They attacked Hanuman from every side with arrows, swords, and spears. Hanuman fought them all at once, using trees, rocks, and his own great strength. All five generals fell, and Hanuman waited calmly for the next foe.
incidents.image: The death of Ravana.jpg

incidents.title: Prince Aksha Is Slain
incidents.story: Young Prince Aksha, Ravana's son, rode out bravely to fight. Hanuman admired the boy's skill and courage and did not wish to harm him, but Aksha's arrows grew more dangerous. At last Hanuman seized him by the feet, whirled him around, and threw him down. Ravana was struck with grief and anger.
incidents.image: Print Ramayana - Pages 49 and 50.jpg

incidents.title: Bound by the Brahmastra
incidents.story: Ravana sent his mightiest son, Indrajit, who used the Brahmastra, the weapon of Brahma, to bind Hanuman. Out of respect for Brahma, Hanuman allowed himself to be held, wanting to meet Ravana face to face. When the demons tied him with ropes, the weapon's hold fell away, but Hanuman stayed calm.
incidents.image: Ravana's son Indrajit is attacking Rama and Lakshmana with arrows that transform into snakes.jpg

incidents.title: Hanuman Before Ravana
incidents.story: Brought before Ravana's dazzling throne, Hanuman was amazed by the king's splendor. Without fear he said he was Rama's messenger and Sugriva's friend. He wisely advised Ravana to return Sita and seek Rama's forgiveness, warning that otherwise Lanka and all its people would be destroyed.
incidents.image: Atikaya, a son of Ravana.jpg

incidents.title: Vibhishana Saves the Messenger
incidents.story: Furious, Ravana ordered that Hanuman be killed. His brother Vibhishana stepped forward and calmly said that killing a messenger is against dharma, the right way of kings. He suggested another punishment instead. Ravana agreed, showing how one good voice could still speak up in an unjust court.
incidents.image: Ravana's son Indrajit is attacking Rama and Lakshmana with arrows that transform into snakes.jpg

incidents.title: The Tail Set on Fire
incidents.story: Ravana ordered Hanuman's tail to be set on fire. The demons wrapped it in cloth, soaked it in oil, lit it, and paraded him through the streets. When Sita heard this, she prayed to Agni, the fire god, to be cool to Hanuman. The fire burned brightly, but it did not hurt him.
incidents.image: Atikaya, a son of Ravana.jpg

incidents.title: Lanka Burns
incidents.story: Hanuman shrank, slipped free of his ropes, and leapt onto the rooftops. With his blazing tail he set fire to palace after palace, and the wind, his father, fanned the flames. He spared the house of the good Vibhishana. Soon golden Lanka glowed with fire, a warning of Rama's coming.
incidents.image: Sita accepting a jewel from Hanumana sent by Rama, 1800s.jpg

incidents.title: Fear for Sita and Relief
incidents.story: Seeing the city in flames, Hanuman suddenly feared that Sita might have been burned too, and he scolded himself for his anger. Then he heard heavenly beings say that Sita was safe. Joyful, he went to see her once more, bowed to her, and promised Rama would come soon.
incidents.image: Indrajita taunts Hanuman as he slays an illusory image of Sita.jpg

incidents.title: The Leap Back Home
incidents.story: Hanuman climbed Mount Arishta, grew huge, and sprang back across the ocean, roaring with joy. On Mount Mahendra, Angada, Jambavan, and the other monkeys heard him and knew he had succeeded. They crowded around him in delight as he told them, Sita has been found.
incidents.image: Rama with the chiefs of his army.jpg

incidents.title: The Feast in Madhuvana
incidents.story: On their happy way back, the monkeys came to Madhuvana, King Sugriva's special honey garden. With Angada's permission they feasted on fruit and honey, danced, and sang to celebrate. In their great joy they grew wild and pushed aside the garden's guards.
incidents.image: The funeral of Bali attended by Tara, Sugriva and Angada (6124580687).jpg

incidents.title: Dadhimukha's Complaint
incidents.story: Dadhimukha, Sugriva's uncle and the keeper of Madhuvana, hurried to Sugriva to complain that the monkeys had spoiled the garden. Instead of being angry, Sugriva smiled. He knew the monkeys would never dare to feast like this unless they had found Sita, and he told Rama the good news.
incidents.image: Sugriva Sends Hanuman to Find Sita, 1981-3-1.jpg

incidents.title: Hanuman Reports to Rama
incidents.story: Hanuman bowed before Rama and said, I have seen Sita. He told of her faithfulness, her suffering, and her message, and placed the hair jewel in Rama's hands. Rama pressed it to his heart and wept, as if Sita herself were near. Hope returned to everyone's hearts.
incidents.image: Raja Sansar Chand and saint Tulsidas paying homage to Rama and Sita.jpg

incidents.title: Rama Embraces Hanuman
incidents.story: When Hanuman returned with news that Sita was alive in Lanka, Rama's heart overflowed. Having no other gift worthy of such service, he held Hanuman in a loving embrace. It was the highest honour Rama could give, and Hanuman treasured it forever.
incidents.image: Hanuman brings Sita Rama's ring (6124590925).jpg

incidents.title: The March to the Southern Sea
incidents.story: At an auspicious hour, Rama set out with Sugriva's great army of monkeys and bears. Nila led the way, finding fruit and water, while Hanuman carried Rama and Angada carried Lakshmana. They crossed forests and mountains until they reached the roaring ocean at Mahendra.
incidents.image: Rama and monkey chiefs.jpg

incidents.title: Ravana Calls His Council
incidents.story: Ashamed that a single monkey had burned his city, Ravana gathered his ministers. Proud generals like Prahasta boasted that they would crush Rama's army easily. Their flattery pleased Ravana, but it led him further away from wisdom and toward his own ruin.
incidents.image: "The Court of Ravana", Folio from a Ramayana MET DP103081.jpg

incidents.title: Vibhishana Pleads for Peace
incidents.story: Ravana's younger brother Vibhishana stood up bravely in the court. He said that stealing Sita was wrong and that Rama was a hero no one could defeat. He begged Ravana to return Sita with honour and save Lanka from destruction.
incidents.image: Rama and monkey chiefs.jpg

incidents.title: Kumbhakarna's Blunt Words
incidents.story: Awake for a short time, the giant Kumbhakarna told Ravana honestly that he had acted without thinking. A wise king takes counsel before he acts, not after. Yet out of love for his brother, Kumbhakarna promised to fight for him anyway.
incidents.image: The Demon Kumbhakarna Is Defeated by Rama and Lakshmana.jpg

incidents.title: Vibhishana Is Insulted and Leaves
incidents.story: When Vibhishana again advised returning Sita, Ravana called him a traitor and an enemy hiding as a brother. Hurt but calm, Vibhishana rose into the sky with four loyal companions. He left Lanka forever, choosing the path of dharma over his brother's pride.
incidents.image: Wat Phra Kaeo mural 2008-09-06 (007).jpg

incidents.title: Rama Grants Refuge to Vibhishana
incidents.story: Some monkeys feared Vibhishana was a spy, but Rama declared that he would never turn away anyone who comes to him for shelter, even an enemy. He welcomed Vibhishana warmly and, right there by the sea, sprinkled him with ocean water as the future king of Lanka.
incidents.image: Vibhishana showing Vimana to Rama.jpg

incidents.title: Rama's Prayer and Anger
incidents.story: Rama lay on a bed of kusha grass for three days, praying to the Ocean to let the army pass. When the sea stayed silent, Rama grew angry and fixed a fiery arrow to his bow. The waters churned, creatures trembled, and the whole world shook in fear.
incidents.image: Rama's Court, Folio from a Ramayana (Adventures of Rama) LACMA AC1999.127.36.jpg

incidents.title: Sagara Rises from the Waves
incidents.story: The Lord of the Ocean rose from the waters with folded hands. He explained that he could not change his own deep nature, but he would hold the waves steady for a bridge. He told Rama that Nala, son of the divine builder Vishvakarma, could build it.
incidents.image: The sons of Sagara discover the stolen sacrificial horse grazing near Vasudeva, who had assumed the form of Kapila 1.jpg

incidents.title: Nala Builds the Bridge
incidents.story: The monkeys uprooted trees and carried boulders and mountain peaks to the shore. Under Nala's skilled guidance they laid them in the sea, and in five days a great bridge stretched all the way to Lanka. The gods and sages looked on in wonder.
incidents.image: Rama's Court, Folio from a Ramayana (Adventures of Rama) LACMA AC1999.127.36.jpg

incidents.title: The Army Crosses to Lanka
incidents.story: With joyful shouts, the vast army of monkeys and bears marched across the bridge over the ocean. Rama and Lakshmana led the way, and soon they camped on the shores of Lanka. The day of reckoning for Ravana had drawn close.
incidents.image: The Celestial Chariot (6124515635).jpg

incidents.title: The Spies Shuka and Sarana
incidents.story: Ravana sent Shuka and Sarana, disguised as monkeys, to count Rama's army. Vibhishana recognised them, but Rama gently let them go and even invited them to see everything. Back in Lanka they praised the monkey heroes, and later the spy Shardula brought the same warning.
incidents.image: Vibhishana bows before Rama.jpg

incidents.title: The Illusory Head of Rama
incidents.story: Hoping to break Sita's spirit, Ravana had a magician create a false head looking just like Rama's, along with his bow. Sita wept bitterly at the sight. But when Ravana was suddenly called away, the head and bow vanished, for they were only a cruel trick.
incidents.image: 19th-century Ramayana manuscript, Rama Thagyin, Myanmar version, Ravana (Dathagiri) dressed as a begging monk to deceive Sita (Thida).jpg

incidents.title: Sarama Comforts Sita
incidents.story: Sarama, a kind rakshasi, came to Sita and told her that Rama was alive and the head was only an illusion. She secretly listened to Ravana's plans and shared them with Sita. Her gentle friendship gave Sita new hope in her darkest hour.
incidents.image: 19th-century Ramayana manuscript, Rama Thagyin, Myanmar version, Ravana (Dathagiri) sends Gambi as golden deer (Shwethamin) to deceive Sita (Thida).jpg

incidents.title: Malyavan's Wise Advice
incidents.story: Ravana's aged grandfather Malyavan warned him that the omens were terrible and that dharma stood with Rama. He urged Ravana to make peace and return Sita. But Ravana rejected the advice angrily and placed his generals at the gates of Lanka.
incidents.image: Sita in the Garden of Lanka.jpg

incidents.title: Rama Sees Lanka from Suvela
incidents.story: Rama and his companions climbed Mount Suvela and gazed upon Lanka. The golden city sat on Mount Trikuta like a city in the sky, with tall towers and beautiful gardens. Rama saw that it was a mighty fortress, but his resolve did not waver.
incidents.image: 19th-century Ramayana manuscript, Rama Thagyin, Myanmar version, Ravana (Dathagiri) sends Gambi as golden deer (Shwethamin) to deceive Sita (Thida).jpg

incidents.title: Sugriva Leaps at Ravana
incidents.story: Spotting Ravana on a tower, Sugriva suddenly leaped across and knocked off his crown. The two wrestled fiercely before Sugriva sprang back to Rama. Rama embraced him but gently scolded him, for a king should not risk his life so rashly.
incidents.image: "Rama Receives Sugriva and Jambavat, the Monkey and Bear Kings", Folio from a Ramayana.jpg

incidents.title: Angada the Envoy
incidents.story: Before the battle, Rama sent Angada to give Ravana a last chance to return Sita. Angada delivered the message boldly. When guards seized him, he leaped onto the palace roof, broke its top with his feet, and flew back to Rama.
incidents.image: Rama's Messenger Angad at the Court of Ravana.jpg

incidents.title: The Battle Begins
incidents.story: The monkeys surrounded Lanka on every side, shouting victory to Rama and Sugriva. They attacked the four gates with trees, rocks, and fists. The rakshasas rushed out with swords and spears, and the great war of the Ramayana began.
incidents.image: Rama Sugriva disscussion about to reach lanka.jpg

incidents.title: Duels of the First Day
incidents.story: Heroes fought one another in single combat. Angada smashed Indrajit's chariot, Hanuman defeated Jambumali, and Nila and Lakshmana struck down mighty foes. Even when night fell, the fierce fighting went on in the darkness, lit only by flashing weapons.
incidents.image: Rama's Messenger Angad at the Court of Ravana.jpg

incidents.title: Indrajit's Serpent Arrows
incidents.story: Indrajit, Ravana's son, made himself invisible and shot arrows that turned into serpents. They bound Rama and Lakshmana tightly, and the brothers fell to the ground. The monkeys were filled with grief, thinking all hope was lost.
incidents.image: Rama Sugriva disscussion about to reach lanka.jpg

incidents.title: Sita Sees the Fallen Brothers
incidents.story: Ravana had Sita flown over the battlefield to see Rama and Lakshmana lying still. Heartbroken, she wept. But the kind rakshasi Trijata comforted her, pointing out that their faces still shone with life and that they were not dead.
incidents.image: Ravana with his Ministers; Sita in the Asoka Grove.jpg

incidents.title: Garuda Frees the Brothers
incidents.story: Suddenly a great wind blew, and Garuda, king of birds, swooped down from the sky. The serpents fled at the sight of him. Garuda gently touched the brothers, healing their wounds and making them stronger than before, and the monkeys cheered.
incidents.image: The Demon Kumbhakarna Is Defeated by Rama and Lakshmana 1.jpg

incidents.title: Dhumraksha Falls
incidents.story: The fierce rakshasa Dhumraksha rode out on a chariot drawn by wolves and lions, and cut down many monkeys. Hanuman faced him and, lifting a huge mountain peak, brought it down upon him. Dhumraksha fell, and the monkeys took heart.
incidents.image: Hanuman Brings the Gandhamardhana Mountain odisha tala patra.jpg

incidents.title: Angada Defeats Vajradamshtra
incidents.story: Next came Vajradamshtra, whose arrows scattered the monkey army. Young Angada stood firm against him. After a long and fierce fight, Angada struck him down with a sword, and the monkeys praised the courage of Vali's son.
incidents.image: Angada smites the demon Narantaka 1.jpg

incidents.title: Hanuman Defeats Akampana
incidents.story: Ravana then sent Akampana, a general famed for never trembling in battle. He fought furiously, but Hanuman uprooted a great tree and struck him with it. Akampana fell, and Ravana began to feel worried for the first time.
incidents.image: 19th-century Ramayana manuscript, Ramakien, Thailand version, Khom script, Hanuman with sword reaches Ravana's palace.jpg

incidents.title: Nila Slays Prahasta
incidents.story: Prahasta, the commander of Ravana's whole army, led a mighty force into battle. Nila, the monkey general, fought him fiercely. When Prahasta charged with his club, Nila lifted a huge rock and struck him down, and the rakshasas fled in fear.
incidents.image: Ramakien 12.jpg

incidents.title: Ravana Takes the Field
incidents.story: With his best generals gone, Ravana himself rode out to fight. He struck Lakshmana with a mighty spear and tried to carry him away, but could not lift him. Hanuman knocked Ravana down with his fist and lovingly carried Lakshmana back to Rama.
incidents.image: "The Court of Ravana", Folio from a Ramayana MET sf2002-505a.jpg

incidents.title: Rama Spares a Weary Ravana
incidents.story: Rama rode on Hanuman's shoulders to face Ravana and shattered his chariot, bow, and crown. Seeing Ravana tired and unarmed, Rama would not strike him. He told Ravana to go home, rest, and return to fight another day. Such was Rama's nobility.
incidents.image: Brooklyn Museum - Ravana Challenges Rama's Army.jpg

incidents.title: Kumbhakarna Is Woken
incidents.story: Desperate, Ravana ordered his giant brother Kumbhakarna woken from his long sleep. Rakshasas beat drums, blew conches, and even marched elephants over him. At last he woke, ate mountains of food, and went to see his brother.
incidents.image: Kumbhakarna, tricked by the gods into asking Brahma for the boon of interminable sleep, slumbers in the magnificent dwelling prepared for him at Ravana's order.jpg

incidents.title: Kumbhakarna Speaks with Ravana
incidents.story: Kumbhakarna told Ravana plainly that he had done wrong and should have listened to good advice. Yet seeing his brother's sorrow, he comforted him. Out of loyalty, he promised to go into battle and fight Rama himself.
incidents.image: Kumbhakarna, the giant brother of Ravana.jpg

incidents.title: Kumbhakarna's Rampage
incidents.story: Kumbhakarna strode onto the battlefield like a walking mountain, crushing and swallowing monkeys. Terrified, the army began to flee. Angada called out to them to stand firm and remember their honour, and the brave ones turned back to fight.
incidents.image: Kumbhakarna in war.jpg

incidents.title: Sugriva Captured and Escaping
incidents.story: Kumbhakarna struck Sugriva down and carried him off toward Lanka. When Sugriva came to his senses, he bit and clawed at the giant, tearing off his ears and nose. In the confusion, Sugriva broke free and sprang back to Rama.
incidents.image: Rama and Lakshmana at Conference with Sugriva, the Simian King, and Companions, Scene from the Story of the Burning of Lanka, Folio from a Ramayana (Adventures of Rama) LACMA M.86.345.14.jpg

incidents.title: Kumbhakarna Slain
incidents.story: Rama faced the giant and cut off his arms and legs with mighty arrows. Then, with an arrow blessed by Indra, he struck off Kumbhakarna's head. The giant fell like a mountain, and the gods rejoiced that the terror had ended.
incidents.image: Killing of Indrajit Painting by Balasaheb Pant Pratinidhi.jpg

incidents.title: Ravana's Grief for Kumbhakarna
incidents.story: When Ravana heard of Kumbhakarna's death, he fell senseless with sorrow. He wept that he had lost his right arm and that life without his brother meant nothing. For the first time, he remembered Vibhishana's warnings with regret.
incidents.image: This painting depicts Kumbhakarna, brother of Ravana.jpg

incidents.title: Ravana's Sons Fall
incidents.story: To comfort their father, Ravana's sons Trishiras, Narantaka, and Devantaka went into battle with their uncles. Angada struck down Narantaka, and Hanuman defeated Devantaka and Trishiras. Nila and Rishabha struck down the uncles Mahodara and Mahaparshva, and one by one Ravana's proud warriors fell.
incidents.image: Manaku - The Monkey Leader Angada Steals Ravana's Crown from His Fortress, Folio from the Siege of Lanka series - 19.24.2 - Metropolitan Museum of Art.jpg

incidents.title: Lakshmana Defeats Atikaya
incidents.story: Atikaya, a giant son of Ravana, wore armour given by Brahma that no ordinary arrow could pierce. Lakshmana fought him long and hard. Then the Wind God whispered advice, and Lakshmana used the Brahmastra to bring Atikaya down.
incidents.image: The golden abode of King Ravana India.jpg

incidents.title: Indrajit's Brahmastra
incidents.story: Furious at his brothers' deaths, Indrajit made himself invisible and released the Brahmastra. Its arrows struck down Rama, Lakshmana, and countless monkeys. Out of respect for Lord Brahma, the brothers did not resist the weapon, and the battlefield fell silent.
incidents.image: Lakshamana fights Indrajit.jpg

incidents.title: Jambavan Sends Hanuman
incidents.story: In the night, Vibhishana and Hanuman searched the battlefield with torches. They found the aged Jambavan, wounded and almost blind, who asked first whether Hanuman lived. If Hanuman lives, he said, we all live. He sent Hanuman to the Himalayas for healing herbs.
incidents.image: Painting of Maharaja Gulab Singh of Kashmir showing reverence to Rama and Sita, Punjab Hills, circa late 19th or early 20th century.png

incidents.title: Hanuman Brings the Herb Mountain
incidents.story: Hanuman flew to the Himalayas, but the magical herbs hid themselves from him. Unwilling to waste time, he lifted the whole mountain peak and carried it back to Lanka. The very fragrance of the herbs healed Rama, Lakshmana, and the entire army.
incidents.image: Hanuman flies to the Himalayas in search of sacred herbs, From the Mewar Ramayana.jpg

incidents.title: Kumbha and Nikumbha Fall
incidents.story: Kumbhakarna's sons Kumbha and Nikumbha came to avenge their father. Kumbha fought Sugriva fiercely, but the monkey king struck him down with his fist. Then Hanuman wrestled the mighty Nikumbha, who swung a great iron club, and defeated him.
incidents.image: Sugriva gains his freedom by his sudden mutilation of Kumbhakarna 1.jpg

incidents.title: Rama Defeats Makaraksha
incidents.story: Makaraksha, son of the demon Khara whom Rama had slain in the forest, came seeking revenge. He challenged Rama boldly. After a fierce duel, Rama struck him down with the fire weapon of Agni, and the rakshasas fled back into Lanka.
incidents.image: Rama strikes down Khara with an arrow 1.jpg

incidents.title: The Illusory Sita Slain
incidents.story: Indrajit created a false Sita by magic and struck her down before Hanuman's eyes. Hanuman rushed back with the terrible news, and Rama fainted with grief. It was a cruel trick meant to break their spirit while Indrajit went to perform a secret ritual.
incidents.image: Sita in Valmiki's hermitage.jpg

incidents.title: Vibhishana Reveals the Secret
incidents.story: Vibhishana assured Rama that Ravana would never let Sita be killed, and the death was only an illusion. He revealed that Indrajit was performing a sacrifice at Nikumbhila that would make him unbeatable. Lakshmana hurried there with Vibhishana and Hanuman to stop it.
incidents.image: Vibhishana meeting Ravana.jpg

incidents.title: Lakshmana Duels Indrajit
incidents.story: Lakshmana interrupted the sacrifice and challenged Indrajit to fight. Their duel was long and terrible, and both were covered with wounds. Arrows filled the sky like rain, and even the gods watched from above, holding their breath.
incidents.image: A battle scene from a manuscript of the Ramayana.jpg

incidents.title: Indrajit Falls
incidents.story: At last Lakshmana fitted the arrow of Indra to his bow and spoke a vow: if Rama is truly righteous and truthful, let this arrow slay Indrajit. The arrow flew and struck off Indrajit's head. Rama embraced his brave brother, and Sushena healed his wounds.
incidents.image: Indrajit worships Devi before battle Lakshmana kills him on the battle field.jpg

incidents.title: Ravana's Rage
incidents.story: Hearing of Indrajit's death, Ravana went mad with grief and anger. He seized a sword and rushed to kill Sita. His wise minister Suparshva stopped him, reminding him that it was shameful to harm a woman, and urged him to face Rama in battle instead.
incidents.image: Victory of Meghanada by RRV.jpg

incidents.title: Ravana's Last Generals Fall
incidents.story: Ravana sent his last commanders to battle. Sugriva struck down Virupaksha and then the mighty Mahodara in fierce duels. Angada slew Mahaparshva with a single blow. Now Ravana had no generals left, and he rode out himself.
incidents.image: "The Court of Ravana", Folio from a Ramayana MET DP107192.jpg

incidents.title: The Shakti Strikes Lakshmana
incidents.story: Ravana hurled a fearsome spear called a Shakti at Vibhishana. To protect his friend, Lakshmana stepped in front, and the spear struck him in the chest. Lakshmana fell, and Rama pulled the spear out with his own hands, weeping for his brother.
incidents.image: Ramakien 00.jpg

incidents.title: Sushena Heals Lakshmana
incidents.story: The monkey physician Sushena sent Hanuman to bring a mountain of healing herbs once more. Sushena crushed the herbs and let Lakshmana breathe their scent. Lakshmana rose, healed and strong, and urged Rama to slay Ravana before the sun set.
incidents.image: Ramakien 09.jpg

incidents.title: Matali Brings Indra's Chariot
incidents.story: Seeing Rama fighting on foot while Ravana rode a chariot, Indra sent his own divine chariot with his charioteer Matali. It shone like the sun and carried heavenly weapons. Rama bowed to it respectfully and climbed aboard for the final battle.
incidents.image: Indra pays homage to Rama after Ravana and his hoards are destroyed (6124524291).jpg

incidents.title: Agastya Teaches Aditya Hridayam
incidents.story: As Rama paused, tired from battle, the great sage Agastya came to him. He taught Rama the Aditya Hridayam, a sacred hymn to the Sun God that gives strength and victory. Rama recited it three times and felt new energy fill his heart.
incidents.image: Killing of Rawana Painting by Balasaheb Pant Pratinidhi.jpg
incidents.artist: Balasaheb Pandit Pant Pratinidhi (author dead before 1952 (A

incidents.title: The Heads That Grew Back
incidents.story: Rama and Ravana fought a duel unlike any other. Each time Rama cut off one of Ravana's heads, a new one grew back in its place. This happened again and again, and Rama wondered how this mighty enemy could be defeated.
incidents.image: Rama launched at his foe a fearsome a bolt.jpg
incidents.artist: Monro, W. D Illustrations by Evelyn Paul

incidents.title: The Brahmastra Is Released
incidents.story: Matali reminded Rama of the Brahmastra, the weapon given to him by the sage Agastya. Rama chanted sacred words and released it. The arrow blazed like fire, filling the sky with light as it flew straight toward Ravana's heart.
incidents.image: Rama slays Shambuka.jpg

incidents.title: Ravana Falls
incidents.story: The Brahmastra pierced Ravana's chest, and he fell from his chariot, never to rise again. Flowers rained from the heavens, and the gods sang Rama's praise. Good had triumphed over evil, and the world was free from fear.
incidents.image: Rama and Lakṣmaṇa attack Ravana, shooting him with many arrows..jpg

incidents.title: Vibhishana Mourns His Brother
incidents.story: Vibhishana wept beside his fallen brother, remembering his strength and greatness. Rama comforted him, saying that enmity ends with death. He told Vibhishana that Ravana was now as dear to him as to Vibhishana, and asked him to perform the last rites with honour.
incidents.image: Vibhishana Meets Rama.jpg
incidents.artist: Ramachandra Madhwa Mahishi Illustrated by Balasaheb Pandit P

incidents.title: Mandodari's Lament
incidents.story: Ravana's queen Mandodari came to the battlefield and wept over her husband. She remembered how mighty he had been, and said that his desire for Sita had brought about his end. Then Vibhishana performed Ravana's funeral with the full honours of a king, as Rama had wished.
incidents.image: Angry Ravana drawing his sword rushed at her to kill Sita.jpg
incidents.artist: by Ramachandra Madhwa Mahishi, Illustrated by Balasaheb Pand

incidents.title: Vibhishana Crowned King of Lanka
incidents.story: Lakshmana anointed Vibhishana as king of Lanka with water from the sea, just as Rama had promised. The rakshasas welcomed their new ruler with joy. Under Vibhishana, Lanka would be guided by dharma and kindness.
incidents.image: Vibhishana shows Rama the two spies who have been caught in their camp.jpg

incidents.title: Hanuman Brings Sita the News
incidents.story: Rama sent Hanuman to tell Sita of the victory. Sita was so overjoyed that at first she could not speak. When Hanuman offered to punish the rakshasis who had troubled her, Sita forgave them, saying that a noble person shows mercy even to those who do wrong.
incidents.image: Angry Ravana drawing his sword rushed at her to kill Sita.jpg
incidents.artist: by Ramachandra Madhwa Mahishi, Illustrated by Balasaheb Pand

incidents.title: Sita's Trial by Fire
incidents.story: Sita was brought before Rama in front of the whole army. Rama spoke stern words about her long stay in Ravana's city. Deeply hurt but firm in her purity, Sita asked Lakshmana to build a fire and, praying to Agni, stepped into the flames.
incidents.image: Wedding of Rama and Sita. Wall painting in Bundi palace, 18 century..jpg

incidents.title: Agni Restores Sita
incidents.story: The fire god Agni rose from the flames holding Sita in his arms, unburnt and shining. He declared that she was pure in thought, word, and deed. Rama joyfully took her back, explaining that he had always known her purity and wanted the world to see it.
incidents.image: The marriage ceremony of Rama and Sita.jpg

incidents.title: Dasharatha Appears from Heaven
incidents.story: Rama's father, King Dasharatha, appeared in a heavenly chariot, glowing with light. He embraced Rama and blessed him, Lakshmana, and Sita. At Rama's request, he forgave Kaikeyi and Bharata, and then returned to the heavenly realm.
incidents.image: The Death of King Dasharatha.jpg

incidents.title: Indra Revives the Monkeys
incidents.story: Indra, king of the gods, offered Rama a boon. Rama asked only that all the monkeys and bears who had died for his cause be brought back to life. Indra granted it, and the fallen warriors rose as if waking from sleep.
incidents.image: Matali invites Rama to raid on Indra's Chariot.jpg

incidents.title: The Flight on Pushpaka
incidents.story: Vibhishana gave Rama the flying Pushpaka chariot, and Rama took his friends with him to Ayodhya. As they flew, Rama showed Sita the battlefield, the great bridge, Kishkindha, and the forests where he had searched for her. Each place held a memory of their journey.
incidents.image: Vibhishana showing Vimana to Rama.jpg

incidents.title: Rama Visits Bharadvaja
incidents.story: On the fifth day after the fourteen years ended, Rama reached the ashram of the sage Bharadvaja. The sage welcomed him lovingly, gave news of Bharata and Ayodhya, and blessed him. Rama stayed the night and prepared to go home.
incidents.image: Rama Visits Bharadvaja's Hermitage, Folio from a Ramayana (Adventures of Rama) LACMA AC1999.127.39.jpg

incidents.title: Hanuman Sent Ahead to Bharata
incidents.story: Rama sent Hanuman ahead to tell Bharata that he was coming home. Hanuman found Bharata at Nandigrama, living simply as a hermit with Rama's sandals on the throne. Bharata was so overjoyed by the news that he embraced Hanuman with tears.
incidents.image: SRI RAMA PATTABHIKSHEKAM WP.jpg

incidents.title: Bharata Welcomes Rama Home
incidents.story: Bharata came to meet Rama with the whole city of Ayodhya. When the brothers met, they embraced with tears of joy. Bharata placed Rama's sandals back on his feet, saying he was returning the kingdom he had kept safe for fourteen years.
incidents.image: Clevelandart 2018.119.jpg

incidents.title: The Coronation of Rama
incidents.story: At last Rama was crowned king of Ayodhya by the sage Vasishtha. Sacred waters from rivers and seas were poured over him, and Sita sat by his side. The people cheered with joy, and the gods sent blessings from above.
incidents.image: Ayodhya celebrates the birth of Rama and his brothers.jpg

incidents.title: Hanuman's Pearl Necklace
incidents.story: After the coronation, Rama gave Sita a beautiful pearl necklace. Sita looked at Rama, and with his gentle nod, she gave it to Hanuman, the one most loyal and brave. Hanuman accepted it with devotion, honoured above all.
incidents.image: Rama gives Ring to Hanuman.jpg

incidents.title: Rama Rajya
incidents.story: Rama ruled Ayodhya with justice and love for many years. In his kingdom no one suffered from hunger, sickness, or fear, and people lived in peace. Rama Rajya became the ideal of a perfect kingdom, remembered for all time.
incidents.image: Sri Rama Become king of Ayodhya.jpg

incidents.title: Agastya Tells of the Rakshasas
incidents.story: After Rama became king, the great sage Agastya came to Ayodhya and told him the old history of the rakshasas. Long ago, the three brothers Malyavan, Sumali and Mali grew mighty and troubled the gods. Vishnu defeated them, and the survivors fled from Lanka to the underworld.
incidents.image: Sita, Lava, and Kusha in the hermitage of Valmiki.jpg

incidents.title: The Birth of Ravana
incidents.story: Sumali wished his family to rise again, so his daughter Kaikasi married the sage Vishrava. She bore Ravana with ten heads, the giant Kumbhakarna, a daughter named Shurpanakha, and the gentle Vibhishana. From one home came very different hearts, and their choices would shape the whole Ramayana.
incidents.image: The demon Kumbhakarna..jpg

incidents.title: The Brothers Win Their Boons
incidents.story: The three brothers performed fierce tapas for thousands of years. Ravana offered his heads one by one, and Brahma granted that no god, demon or spirit could kill him, though in his pride he did not ask for safety from humans. Kumbhakarna was given long sleep, and Vibhishana asked always to love dharma.
incidents.image: Agni Pariksha.jpg

incidents.title: Ravana Seizes Lanka and Pushpaka
incidents.story: Lanka was then ruled by Kubera, Ravana's half-brother and the lord of wealth. Proud of his boon, Ravana demanded the golden city, and Kubera left it peacefully on their father's advice. Later Ravana attacked Kubera, defeated him in battle, and took his flying chariot, the Pushpaka.
incidents.image: Surpanakha showing her bleeding cut nose to her elder brother Ravana, the king of Lanka.jpg

incidents.title: Ravana Lifts Mount Kailasa
incidents.story: Flying over Kailasa, Ravana's chariot suddenly stopped, and Nandi warned him that Shiva dwelt there. In anger, Ravana pushed his arms under the mountain and lifted it. Shiva gently pressed down with his toe, trapping Ravana's arms. His loud cry earned him the name Ravana, and after long praise Shiva released him.
incidents.image: Ravana Receiving a Boon from Shiva LACMA M.2009.148.2.jpg

incidents.title: The Curse of Vedavati
incidents.story: In the Himalayan forest, Ravana met Vedavati, a pure maiden doing tapas to win Vishnu as her husband. When he seized her by the hair, she cut it off and entered a fire. Before leaving her body, she vowed to be born again to bring about his ruin, and it is said she was reborn as Sita.
incidents.image: Kerta Gosa, Ramayana Scene, Bali 1544.jpg

incidents.title: Indrajit Captures Indra
incidents.story: Ravana marched on heaven and fought the gods. When the battle turned against his father, Ravana's son Meghanada used his magic to vanish, bound Indra, and carried him to Lanka. Brahma came to free Indra and gave the young warrior the name Indrajit, conqueror of Indra.
incidents.image: Victory-of-indrajit.jpg

incidents.title: Kartavirya Arjuna Defeats Ravana
incidents.story: By the Narmada river, Ravana sat worshipping Shiva with flowers. Upstream, the thousand-armed king Kartavirya Arjuna held back the water while playing, and the flood swept Ravana's offerings away. Ravana attacked in rage, but the king overpowered him and kept him captive until the sage Pulastya asked for his release.
incidents.image: Kusha Kills Lakshmana.jpg

incidents.title: Vali Carries Ravana Across the Seas
incidents.story: Ravana wished to fight Vali, the mighty vanara king, and crept up behind him while he prayed by the southern ocean. Vali simply tucked Ravana under his arm and flew to all four oceans to finish his prayers. Humbled, Ravana asked for friendship, and they became allies.
incidents.image: Ravana encounters a fearsome door guardian at Vali's palace.jpg

incidents.title: Baby Hanuman Leaps at the Sun
incidents.story: As a hungry baby, Hanuman saw the rising sun and thought it was a ripe fruit. He leapt into the sky to catch it. Indra struck him with his thunderbolt, hurting his jaw, and his angry father Vayu stopped the air from moving. The gods then healed Hanuman and blessed him with many great powers.
incidents.image: JAGJIVAN LAL Indra shoot hanuman.jpg

incidents.title: Hanuman Forgets His Strength
incidents.story: Young Hanuman was so full of energy that he played pranks on the sages in their hermitages. The sages lovingly cursed him to forget his powers until someone reminded him. That is why, much later, Jambavan had to remind him of his strength before his great leap to Lanka.
incidents.image: Hanuman fells Jambumali.jpg

incidents.title: The Friends Return Home
incidents.story: When the coronation festivities ended, Rama gave rich gifts to Sugriva, Vibhishana, Angada, Jambavan and all the vanaras and rakshasas who had helped him. With tears of love, they took leave of him. Each returned to his own kingdom, carrying the memory of Rama's kindness.
incidents.image: "Rama Receives Sugriva and Jambavat, the Monkey and Bear Kings", Folio from a Ramayana MET 2002.503.jpg

incidents.title: Hanuman's Wish
incidents.story: As he took leave, Hanuman asked Rama for one gift. He wished that his love for Rama would never fade, and that he might live on earth for as long as Rama's story is told. Rama gladly granted it and embraced him, saying he could never repay Hanuman's service.
incidents.image: Hanuman approaches Rama and Lakshmana in the guise of an ascetic.jpg

incidents.title: Sita's Wish to Visit the Hermitages
incidents.story: Rama and Sita spent happy days in the palace gardens of Ayodhya. When Sita was expecting a child, Rama asked what she wished for. She longed to visit the peaceful hermitages of the sages on the banks of the Ganga, and Rama promised that she would go.
incidents.image: Raja Ravi Varma, Sree Rama Crossing Sarayu river.jpg

incidents.title: The Talk in the City
incidents.story: Rama asked his friend Bhadra what the people of Ayodhya were saying about him. Bhadra replied that they praised his victory, but some doubted Sita because she had lived in Ravana's palace. Later tellings say Rama overheard a washerman, but in Valmiki the news comes through Bhadra, and it deeply troubles the king.
incidents.image: Popular print, album (BM 2003,1022,0.49 1).jpg

incidents.title: Rama's Painful Decision
incidents.story: Rama called his brothers and, with a heavy heart, told them of the people's talk. Though he knew Sita was pure, he felt a king must keep the trust of his people. He asked Lakshmana to take Sita to the hermitages she wished to see and leave her near Valmiki's ashram.
incidents.image: Rama, Sita and Lakshmana at the hermitage.jpg

incidents.title: Lakshmana Leaves Sita by the Ganga
incidents.story: Lakshmana drove Sita to the Ganga and took her across the river. There, weeping, he told her Rama's command. Sita was heartbroken, yet she sent Rama a gentle message to rule his people well, and said she carried his child. Lakshmana bowed to her and sadly returned.
incidents.image: Indian School, late 18th century - Rama and Sita with Hanuman and Lakshman. - RCIN 1005113.ac - Royal Collection.jpg

incidents.title: Valmiki Shelters Sita
incidents.story: The young sons of the sages saw Sita weeping alone and ran to tell Valmiki. The kind sage came at once, comforted her, and said he knew she was innocent. He led her to the women of the hermitage, who welcomed and cared for her like a daughter.
incidents.image: Hermitage of Valmiki, Folio from the "Nadaun" Ramayana (Adventures of Rama) LACMA AC1999.127.45.jpg

incidents.title: The Birth of Lava and Kusha
incidents.story: On the night Shatrughna stayed at Valmiki's hermitage, Sita gave birth to twin sons. Valmiki protected the babies with blessings using sacred kusha grass. The elder, touched with the tips of the grass, was named Kusha, and the younger, touched with its lower part, was named Lava.
incidents.image: Lava, one of Rāma’s sons..jpg

incidents.title: Shatrughna Slays Lavanasura
incidents.story: The sages of the Yamuna forest asked Rama for help against Lavana, a cruel rakshasa who held Shiva's mighty trident. Rama sent Shatrughna with a divine arrow. Shatrughna waited at the gate so Lavana could not reach his trident, then slew him. He founded the city of Madhura, later called Mathura, and ruled it well.
incidents.image: Rama and his brothers in the company of Raja Dashratha and his three queens.jpg

incidents.title: The Ashvamedha with a Golden Sita
incidents.story: Rama performed the great horse sacrifice in the Naimisha forest by the Gomati river. Kings and sages came from everywhere. Rama never took another wife, so a golden image of Sita sat beside him in her place, showing his lifelong faithfulness to her.
incidents.image: Rama asks Sita to prove her chastity and integrity by entering fire.jpg
incidents.artist: Chitra Ramayana by Ramachandra Madhwa Mahishi, Illustrated b

incidents.title: Lava and Kusha Capture the Horse
incidents.story: In later tellings, such as the Padma Purana and Jaimini's Ashvamedha, Lava and Kusha caught the sacrificial horse in the forest and refused to let it go. They bravely fought the warriors sent to win it back. This story is not found in Valmiki's Ramayana, but it is loved across India.
incidents.image: Kusha and Lava chant the poem before Rama.jpg

incidents.title: Lava and Kusha Sing the Ramayana
incidents.story: Valmiki sent Lava and Kusha to sing his poem at Rama's sacrifice. Dressed as young ascetics, they sang the Ramayana so sweetly that the whole assembly listened in wonder. Rama offered them gold, but they gently refused, saying they lived in the forest and needed nothing.
incidents.image: Lava-Kush tying the sacrificial horse to a banana tree in the hermitage of sage Valmiki based on the story of the Epic Ramayana, 1820 CE, Kangra School of Art, National Museum Delhi.jpg

incidents.title: Rama Recognises His Sons
incidents.story: As the twins sang day after day, Rama learned that they were the sons of Sita. His heart was filled with love and longing. He sent messengers to Valmiki, asking Sita to come before the assembly and declare her purity so that the people would accept her.
incidents.image: Laxman meets Rama after sita exile.jpg

incidents.title: Sita Returns to the Earth
incidents.story: Valmiki led Sita into the assembly and declared that she was pure. Sita said that if she had never thought of anyone but Rama, Mother Earth should receive her. The ground opened, the Earth goddess rose on a divine throne, took Sita in her arms, and vanished as flowers fell from the sky.
incidents.image: Parshurama rama.jpg

incidents.title: The Passing of the Queens
incidents.story: Rama ruled for many years in grief and duty. In time, his mothers Kausalya, Sumitra and Kaikeyi grew old and left this world. Having lived lives of devotion, they joined King Dasharatha in heaven, and Rama honoured them with sacred rites and gifts.
incidents.image: Rama Bestows His Possessions on the Brahmins, His Friends, and Servants, Folio from the "Shangri" Ramayana.jpg

incidents.title: Kingdoms for the Princes
incidents.story: Bharata conquered the land of the Gandharvas and founded the cities of Takshashila and Pushkalavati for his sons Taksha and Pushkala. Lakshmana's sons Angada and Chandraketu were given kingdoms in the land of Karupatha. In this way, Rama's family spread his just rule far and wide.
incidents.image: Court Artist Draws the Portraits of Bharata and Shatrughna.jpg

incidents.title: Time Visits Rama
incidents.story: One day Kala, the spirit of Time, came to Rama dressed as an ascetic with a message from Brahma. He asked to speak alone, and Rama ordered that anyone who disturbed them must be given up. Lakshmana stood guard. Kala gently reminded Rama that his work on earth was complete.
incidents.image: The worship of Shiva, Vishnu and Brahma (6124593967).jpg

incidents.title: Lakshmana's Great Sacrifice
incidents.story: The fiery sage Durvasa came and demanded to see Rama at once, threatening to curse the whole kingdom. To save everyone, Lakshmana entered the room, knowing the price. To keep his word, Rama gave up his beloved brother. Lakshmana went calmly to the Sarayu and left his body, and the gods welcomed him to heaven.
incidents.image: 13 Rama, Sita and Lakshman seated by a rocky shore. ca. 1820, San Diego Museum of Art.jpg

incidents.title: Rama's Last Journey
incidents.story: Rama crowned Kusha and Lava as kings and walked to the Sarayu, followed by Bharata, Shatrughna, and the people of Ayodhya. Entering the sacred river, Rama returned to his divine form as Vishnu. All who had followed him with love were given a place in heaven, while Hanuman stayed on earth.
incidents.image: Valmiki instructs Kusha and Lava in the recitation of the Ramayana before the occasion of a sacrifice in Rama's palace(1).jpg
